*vastu* line [nn], folio number.
[1a1] This is the *Vinayasūtra* composed by the master Guṇaprabha. Written by Śrīlāka. Bhadantaguṇaprabhaviracitaṃ *Vinayasūtram*. (62 folio).
The Vinaya Sūtra of the Mūlasarvāstivādins:
The Section on Going Forth (*Pravrajyāvastu*)
**(Vin_1,1) The Ordination into the State of a Śrāmaṇera [1b1] / Homage to the Buddha / Vin_1.1 / Now follows the account of the Going Forth.**

Vin_1.2. When the entire Saṃgha has assembled, having assumed this attire, with palms joined and squatting at the end of the senior monks, he should request ordination; then, by means of a formal act consisting of one motion and three proclamations (*jñapticaturtha-karman*), they should confer upon him both the going-forth (*pravrajyā*) and full ordination (*upasampadā*). This is the ancient rule.
Vin_1.3. For one who has gone forth, a certain monk should serve as his preceptor (*upādhyāya*) there for the sake of the going-forth and full ordination.
Vin_1.4: Having asked about the obstructing factors (*antarāyika*), one should grant permission for the status of a former preceptor (*pūrvopādhyāya*) to one who is pure.
Vin_1.5: For one who has not previously entered [the lower stages], there is no subsequent [ordination] into the states of a lay follower (*upāsaka*), a novice (*śrāmaṇera*), or a monk (*bhikṣu*).
Vin_1.6: One should perform the formal declaration of undertaking the state of a lay follower or a novice, beginning with the words of accepting the going for refuge (*śaraṇagati*).
Vin_1.7. Immediately following this, there is the proclamation of the training rules by way of formal acceptance.
Vin_1.8. Having personally led [the candidate] to the status of a lay follower (*upāsaka*), one should hand him over to the community for its announcement to a monk.
Vin_1.9. Having asked, "Is he pure? and having ascertained that he is pure, one should announce his purity.
Vin_1.10: Or, when everyone has assembled, they may perform the *anulayana* (the formal inquiry).
Vin_1.11: If [the candidate] is pure, they should all say, "He is pure.
Vin_1.12: He should then request a preceptor (*upādhyāya*).
Vin_1.13 / He should have the hair and beard shaved, leaving a tuft.
Vin_1.14 / When asked, "Let the tuft be shaved," and permission is granted, [he should shave] it.
Vin_1.15 / He should bathe.
Vin_1.16. The preceptor shall give the saffron-colored robes.
Vin_1.17. Having prostrated at his feet, [the candidate] shall accept them. Vin_1.18. The preceptor shall then put them on.
One should examine the literal phrasing, provided it was not intended [as a definitive statement].
One should lead [the candidate] to the going forth, beginning with the taking of the refuges (Vin 1.21),
or immediately after the instruction (Vin 1.22).
One should cause the monk who leads [him] to the state of a śrāmaṇera to exert himself.
Vin_1.23: Having asked, "Is someone pure? one should bring forward one who is pure.
Vin_1.24: He is the preceptor (ācārya).
Vin_1.25: And [there are] the private instructor, the one who performs the formal act, the one who provides reliance, and the reciter.
Vin_1.26: When the matter has been accomplished, there is the state of it having occurred.
Vin_1.27: When the preceptor has accepted the instruction, that [instruction] arises.
Vin_1.28: Upon the completion of the third *āvṛtti*, there is the state of having been accomplished in the final part.
Vin_1.29: For example, at the time of proclaiming another's [virtues], [the proclamation] of the state of a *śrāmaṇera* [is required].
Vin_1.30: At the end [of the proclamation], that of the status of a preceptor (*upādhyāya*).
Vin_1.31: The limit for the granting of the supreme good (*niḥśreyasa*) is to attend upon [the teacher] as one’s reliance (*niḥśraya*) for one night.
Vin_1.32: Reciting means repeating a single verse three times. Vin_1.33: There is no status of "recitation" in uttering [a text] with the intention of not reciting it. Vin_1.34:
One should not apply these two [terms] otherwise.
One should not do so for another.
Without first saying, "I shall mention the name for the sake of the matter," one should not mention the name of the preceptor.
This is the procedure for the initiation into the state of a *śrāmaṇera*.
**(Vin_1,2) The Procedure for Full Ordination (Upasaṃpad-vidhi)** Vin_1.37: Full ordination is from the Saṃgha. Vin_1.38:

Having turned his attention toward the status of having a preceptor (upādhyāya), he should request a monk to act as the officiator of the ritual (karmakāraka) and a monk to act as the private instructor (raho ’nuśāsaka).
Vin_1.39. He should request a preceptor. Vin_1.40. The preceptor himself should cause him to formally dedicate the three robes.
Vin_1.41. Having displayed the bowl, he should observe silence.
"Shame on him who causes a Pandu-peti!"—thus [they speak] regarding the Saṃgha.
(Vin 1.42) "A good bowl"—thus they should all say, not otherwise.
(Vin 1.43) Having identified the one who has stepped aside, having encouraged the one who instructs in private, the performer of the ritual action should cause the Saṃgha to authorize him.
Vin_1.44: He should instruct him in private, saying, "Listen, you.
Vin_1.45: Having said to him, "Stay; do not go when called," and having instructed him, he should report his purity to the Saṃgha and ask, "Shall he come?
Vin_1.46: If they all say, "He is pure," [then he may enter].
The officiant of the formal act (karmakāraka) should request ordination (upasaṃpad).
Having made it known, he should inquire regarding the obstacles to the Saṃgha.
He should then lead [the candidate] to the full ordination.
Vin_1.50: One should have the shadow measured immediately thereafter.
Vin_1.51: It is best to do this with a four-fingered stick.
Vin_1.52: He is designated by the term "man" (puruṣa).
Vin_1.53 / [The divisions of] the day and night, beginning with the forenoon (pūrvāhṇa) and so forth.
Vin_1.54 / And these five [types of] occasions (samaya). Vin_1.55 / The winter, the summer, the rainy season, the limited rainy season, and the long rainy season.
Vin_1.56. The first two [periods] are four months each.
Vin_1.57. The next is one month.
Vin_1.58. After that, it is by day and night.
Vin_1.59. That which is deficient shall be for a final period of three months.
Vin_1.60. One should announce the formal supports (niḥśraya). Vin_1.61. [One should announce] the offenses involving defeat (pātayantikā-dharmas).

Vin_1.62 And [he should instruct him] in the practices that make one a śramaṇa. Vin_1.63 Having grasped the perfection and correctness of what is sought, he should enjoin him toward the attainment of the commonality of moral discipline within the assembly.
Vin_1.64 [He should do so] by reflecting upon the connection with the means of subsistence.
Vin_1.65 / Regarding living in communion with one who has been disciplined;

Vin_1.66 / regarding the performance of what is necessary; Vin_1.67 / he should explain the state of being in the process of attainment to one who does not know that the undertaking has been completed.
Vin_1.68: One should enjoin [the candidate] with respect.
Vin_1.69: And there is the narration of the means for its accomplishment; this is the procedure for full ordination (*upasaṃpad-vidhi*).
(k) Regarding dependence:
(Vin 1.70) One who is dependent [upon a teacher] should not perform any duty without first looking back at that teacher.
(Vin 1.71) This applies except when voiding excrement or urine.
Vin_1.72: The discarding of the tooth-stick; and the worship of the Caitya within the monastery precincts.

Vin_1.73: Traveling from the monastery for less than fifty *vyāmas*; [the following involve] intense eagerness: regarding the work of the bowl and robes, attendance upon the sick, the dispelling of remorse, and the relinquishing of evil views.
"If only I could fall into such a state that I might do it or cause it to be done" (Vin 1.74);

or, when desiring to make a formal resolution (*praṇidhāna*) within the Saṅgha, thinking, "Oh, would that the Saṅgha would not perform this act of resolution" (Vin 1.75); or, once [the act] has been performed, one should remain [in that state].

Vin_1.76. To one who requests the turning back (*āvartana*) of probation (*parivāsa*), initial probation (*mūlaparivāsa*), re-integration (*mānāpya*), or initial re-integration (*mūlamānāpya*), the *niḥśraya* (preceptor) should say: "Alas! May the Saṃgha grant you the fourfold [penances] beginning with probation, and may it lift them.
Vin_1.77. He too should do this for him, setting aside the formal inquiry (*avalokana*). Vin_1.78.

One who is less than ten years [of standing] shall not perform the functions of ordination (*upasaṃpadā*), acting as a preceptor (*upādhyāya*), acting as a *niḥśraya*, or residing under the dependence (*niḥśrita-vāsa*) of another.
Vin_1.79. Not with anyone who lacks [the necessary qualities], but through association with those who are proximate.

Vin_1.80. For the purpose of the boundary, regarding the performance or causing the performance of nursing the sick, dispelling remorse, abandoning evil views, and the non-delighting in the state of indolence. Vin_1.81.
Because of the nature of being a field of merit (*puṇyakṣetra*), even among those who do not possess the five [qualities], there is virtue and great learning.
Vin_1.82: Mastery of the Piṭakas; Vin_1.83: Possessing the capability to cause others to grasp them;
Vin_1.84: Training in the higher training of virtue, mind, and wisdom.
Vin_1.85: Or, [he is qualified] by being capable of training [others].
Vin_1.86: Thus is the *adhyācāra-vinaya-prātimokṣa*.
Vin_1.87: [He is qualified] by being endowed with faith, ethical discipline, learning, generosity, and wisdom.
Virtue, concentration, wisdom, liberation,
and the knowledge and vision [of liberation];
as well as the state of having initiated vigor and the state of being wise.
Vin_1.90 / Possessing mindfulness; Vin_1.91 / Being withdrawn in seclusion; Vin_1.92 / Being concentrated in meditative absorption.

The state of being a learner (śaikṣatva); the state of being one beyond learning (aśaikṣatā); and mastery regarding arising, designation, subsequent designation, prohibition, permission, and supernormal knowledge (abhijñā).

Vin_1.96: The quality of being an instructor who, having understood what constitutes an obstacle and what does not constitute an obstacle, makes this known. Vin_1.97: The quality of being capable of providing instruction, whether as a formal reliance (*niḥśraya*) or a non-reliance, together with the ability to grasp [the teachings].
Vin_1.98: The quality of possessing knowledge regarding the gravity or lightness of an offense, and of being one who has practiced the detailed exposition of the *Prātimokṣa*.

Vin_1.99. In the absence of an elder, one should rely on a junior. Vin_1.100. One should not entirely neglect the proper conduct of reverence. Vin_1.101. One who has completed five years of seniority may wander through the countryside, provided he is not without reliance and is endowed with the final set of [disciplinary] rules.
Even one who possesses the threefold knowledge is not [qualified] for the status of a *niḥśraya* (spiritual preceptor).
(kha) Pertaining to those to be admitted: Vin_1.103. One who has approached for the sake of going forth, saying "I am a heretic," should be questioned; and so too should the ordainers. Vin_1.104.

They should not, having rejected one whose mind is not satisfied, allow a Śākya or an Āgneya matted-hair ascetic to go forth or receive full ordination, with the exception of those heretics who have already satisfied [the Teacher] and so forth, up to the end of the list of heretics.
Vin_1.105. When one speaks truthfully of the praise of the jewels and the blame of the non-Buddhists, there is no resentment and the mind is propitiated.

Vin_1.106. For that purpose, the Saṃgha should grant him a probation (*parivāsa*) for four months by means of a formal act (*karman*), even though he does not possess those qualities, once he has completed his status as a lay follower (*upāsaka*). Vin_1.107. His food shall be provided by the Saṃgha.

Vin_1.108 / [He may accept] a robe from the preceptor. Vin_1.109 / And [the preceptor] has the status of agent regarding the undertaking of the formal act. Vin_1.110 / One who has approached for the purpose of going forth should be asked, "Are you full fifteen years of age?"
Vin_1.111. They should not ordain one who is less than seven years old, whether he is incapable or capable of flying away like a crow.
Vin_1.112. One should not cause a novice (śramaṇoddeśa) to attend upon oneself for more than one year.
Vin_1.113. If there is no desire [to remain], and if he has been ordained more than once, one should provide him with what is beyond the requirements of ordination.
Vin_1.114. If [the candidate] is deficient [in years], one may entrust him to another for the purpose of relying upon [a teacher].
Vin_1.115. That person must not deprive him [of that status].
Vin_1.116. One should confer full ordination; even if he does not offer it, one should take hold of him by force and act with resolve.
Vin_1.117: When someone is away, something—whether little or much—should be given to them.
Vin_1.118: One whose father is living should not go forth without his permission. Vin_1.119: One who desires the going-forth and is not far from those two [parents] may be kept for seven days.
Vin_1.120: One should not ordain this person into the Saṃgha without having informed [the parents], even if they reside in a distant land.
Vin_1.121: It is proper for the Saṃgha to provide food to one who seeks ordination. Vin_1.122: Once permission has been granted by his parents, he may leave them behind and go to a distant land.
Vin_1.123. When someone has approached [the preceptor] saying, "I am ill," he should ask him. Vin_1.124. Or he should ask, "Do you have any illness at all? Vin_1.125.
This is especially so in the case of those who are to be ordained.
Vin_1.126: They should not ordain one who is ill, nor should they confer full admission upon such a person.
Vin_1.127: [This applies] until the formal resolution has been made.
Vin_1.128 / And there is no quality of sprouting for this. Vin_1.129 / Thus is the destruction of one who possesses the marks. Vin_1.130 / [He is] a created being (nirmita).
Vin_1.131 / A paṇḍaka (eunuch).

Vin_1.132 / There are five types of this [condition]: innate, one who manifests [impotence] due to attachment to a side, one who has fallen into calamity through envy, one who has been rendered so by a blow, and one who has become so through disease.
Vin_1.133 / In this case, if the last [type] partakes of the fault, there is no loss [of the vow].
One who lives in association with a thief:

knowing that the formal act of ordination has been performed or that it has taken root, yet not having participated in the ritual action together with the second assembly—this is the reality [of the offense].
One who has entered the ranks of the heretics (tīrthika). Vin 1.134.
Vin_1.135. This [occurs] for one who has undertaken the going-forth and holds that view; having cast aside this robe, by means of that banner, at the rising of dawn therein, that is the reality.
Vin_1.136. If it is not done, there is the meaning of theft, as in the case of stealing.
Vin_1.137. A matricide.
Vin_1.138 / A matricide;
Vin_1.139 / A patricide;
Vin_1.140 / A schismatic of the Saṃgha.
One who, with a malicious mind, has caused the blood of a Tathāgata to flow;
one who has violated a nun;
or one who has committed any one of the four *pārājika* offenses.

If there were an undertaking, there would be a collection [of causes]; furthermore, it is a formal vow. If one speaks falsely regarding the failure to see [an offense], it is an offense requiring expiation (prāyaścittika).
[Those who have] hands severed, feet severed, or fingers like the hood of a snake;

Those who have not performed the *aṣṭakā* rites, those with variegated limbs, the very old, and the very young; the lame, the one with a withered arm, the one-eyed, the one with a crooked hand, or the hunchbacked;
those with goiters, the mute, the deaf, those who crawl on a board, and those with elephantiasis.
Those men who are severed by women, severed by burdens, and severed from the path;
those who have been called "palmyra trees" and "severed kandalī stalks"—such persons were indeed rejected by the Great Seer.
But for one who is pleasing, the going forth and the pure higher ordination are appropriate.
Thus has it been declared by the Perfectly Awakened One, who knows all and whose name is Truth;
the section on ordination, including what is to be included and its conclusion, is finished.
(Vin_1,3) Included in the *Kṣudraka* section:
Vin_1.146 // A king’s soldier.
Vin_1.147 / Not permitted by the king, and located not far away.
Vin_1.148: One who has had a hand cut off is like a murderer bearing a flag.
Vin_1.149: One should not grant the going forth to chariot-makers, caṇḍālas, pukkasas, or those of similar castes.
Vin_1.150: Those with severed hands and so forth are given as examples.
Those with turmeric-colored hair, golden hair, and likewise green hair; those with white hair, those with serpent-like hair, and those who are hairless;
those with protruding skulls, those with heads like the *badara* fruit, those who are excessively corpulent, and those with flattened heads.
Some had the heads of donkeys or pigs, some had two heads, and some were headless;
they had ears like those of elephants, horses, or monkeys, or ears like those of donkeys and pigs;
some had only one ear, and some were earless.
Those with red eyes, those with very large eyes, those with small eyes, and those that are deep yellow;
those with glass-like eyes, those with eyes like bubbles, those with a single eye, and even those without eyes;
those with the noses of elephants, horses, oxen, and mṛgaṭas.
They have noses like those of donkeys and pigs; some have a single nose, while others have no nose at all.
They have jaws like those of elephants, horses, oxen, mṛgaṭas, donkeys, and pigs;
some have a single jaw, while others have no jaw at all.
Those with tusks like elephants, horses, oxen, or mṛgaṭa deer;
those with tusks like donkeys or pigs; those with a single tusk or no tusks at all;
those with excessively long necks, no necks, shoulders like axles, or who are hunchbacked.
Those with severed tails, those with testicles like wind-bags, those with only one testicle, and those without testicles;
those who are excessively tall or excessively short, those who are emaciated, and those who suffer from extreme leprosy;
and those with four different skin colors, as well as those who are dribbling and deformed.
One should maintain such a rejection even toward one who is of this kind.
(Vin 1.151) One should not attend upon a renunciant who is corrupted by birth or body.
(Vin 1.152) It is not appropriate for one person to receive the taking up [of the precepts] from a single preceptor with a single word, unless there is a specific reason. (Vin 1.153)
Vin_1.153. There is no mutual performance of respectful salutation (sāmīcī) among those who have attained equal status.
Vin_1.154. Seniority is determined by the time of ordination.
Vin_1.155. A forest-dweller (āraṇyaka) shall not wear hair longer than two finger-breadths.

Vin_1.156. This [practice] does not apply to one who lives near a village because of his proximity. Vin_1.157. One should not have the hair cut like cow-hair. Vin_1.158. Except for the area around a wound.
Vin_1.159: One should not have a topknot made. Vin_1.160: One should not perform hair-removal on the private parts.
Vin_1.161: One may have it done for the sake of a wound, provided it has not healed; otherwise, one should do so after observing the elder monks.
Vin_1.162: One should not direct one's attention toward the veins of a woman as a basis for meditation.
Vin_1.163: Nor elsewhere on the body; nor should one employ a razor-sharp edge, a nail-cutter, or the blade of an axe.
Vin_1.164: One should not practice the polishing of these [tools].
Vin_1.165. One should apply a comb for the removal of dirt, but one should not shave the hair and beard with a robe.
Vin_1.166. One should keep a hair-catcher; in its absence, one may use a *saṃkakṣikā*. Vin_1.167. [End of section 167.]
Vin_1.168: Not on a spread of grass.
Vin_1.169: Not where the broom belonging to the Saṃgha is kept.
Vin_1.170: One who is aged, ill, or [exposed] to wind, heat, and rain may set it down out of necessity.
Vin_1.171. One should prepare that area.
Vin_1.172. In a crowded place, there is the cutting of hair.
Vin_1.173. Likewise for the clipping of nails.
Vin_1.174. A nun who has not been supervised by a man free from passion must not have her hair cut.

Vin_1.175. If she becomes lustful, the supervisor should instruct her: "Establish mindfulness; what essence is there in this putrid carcass? Vin_1.176. She should regard the barber as a mother, a sister, or a daughter.
Vin_1.177. Having bathed, one should perform [the ritual purification]. Vin_1.178. Or one may perform the five-limbed purification; one should not bathe naked. Vin_1.179.
A nun should not use powder at a bathing place for men, nor at a bathing place for women.
Vin_1.180: It is permissible to use powder that has been infused with the scent of *mudga* beans and the like.
Vin_1.181: There is permission for its acceptance. Vin_1.182: And [it is permissible] for one who is ill to use that which has been infused with medicine.
Vin_1.183: A nun shall not throw powder at a woman.
Vin_1.184: She shall not ascend a ladder whose rungs are not tied together and whose ends are not covered from front to back.
Vin_1.185: It shall not be otherwise than thus.
Vin_1.186. One should not resort to a covering that does not conceal the face.
Vin_1.187. One should wear a bathing cloth.
Vin_1.188. There is an attachment of living beings to a double-layered [cloth].
Even one who possesses only the three robes [is permitted to bathe].
(Vin 1.189) Having placed the bowls in front and behind, one should bathe in a secluded place.
(Vin 1.190) If a living being becomes stuck due to the discharge [of semen], it must be removed.
Vin_1.191: This refers to a monastery situated on a water-encircled island. Vin_1.192: And there is the removal of liquid.
Vin_1.193: The construction of a bathhouse.
Vin_1.194: The laying of bricks for it;
the release of the water-channel.
Vin_1.195: Cleansing the drainage channel.
Vin_1.196: When one has bathed in a whirlpool, there is no requirement to rise [immediately].
Vin_1.197: One should cleanse the body by rubbing with a brush, but not with the feet.
This is an illustration regarding those who are fierce and arrogant.
(Vin 1.199) Purifying sour gruel with fire.
(Vin 1.200) No one shall rub a nun with a cloth-wick held in a fist.
Vin_1.201. One should not put on the robes while the water has not yet lost its turbidity.
Vin_1.202. One should carry a body-wiping cloth.
Vin_1.203. In its absence, having stood for a moment with a *kuṭuka* (a small vessel), one should wipe oneself with a bathing-cloth.

Vin_1.204: One may use a steam bath (jentāka). Vin_1.205: It is good to construct a sauna (karaṇḍa) on ground free of gravel. Vin_1.206: It should be shaped like the ocean—narrowed on the outside and wide on the inside—with an opening for the smoke in the middle.
Vin_1.207. Herein, there is the installation of lattices, windows, small door-panels, pivots, bolts, and pins.
Vin_1.208. And there is the setting up of goat-footed supports and staffs.
Vin_1.209. At the door, there is the fitting of the door-panel, the bolt, the socket, and the cross-bar.
Vin_1.210: A pigeon-hole should be constructed on the inner wall for the purpose of storing heated water.
Vin_1.211: In the place where fire is used, bricks should be laid upon the ground.
Vin_1.212: This is for the purpose of ensuring that [the fire] does not go out.
Vin_1.213. For that purpose, one should carry an iron buttock-padded seat.
Vin_1.214. When the fire is blazing, one should avoid entering it so as not to become exhausted.
Vin_1.215. To prevent the occurrence of darkness, one should throw roasted barley flour smeared with pungent oil into the fire.

Vin_1.216 / Incense should be offered to eliminate foul odors. Vin_1.217 / A provision is made for rapid clearing [of obstructions] by means of a ball of *cikkasa* (a type of plant). Vin_1.218 / One should frighten away those who cook balls of *āmalaka* or balls of *pācakakṣa*.
Vin_1.219: [The ground] is made into a mere covering by grass, or by its natural moisture, or by moistening it.
Vin_1.220: A ladle-shaped instrument is made for the purpose of scratching.
Vin_1.221: Having inserted it through a hole, it is fixed with a cord by the attendant of the requisites in a concealed place.
Vin_1.222. For the sake of perfecting the power of transformation, the preparation of a fire-like state is performed in this [state].
Vin_1.223. Therein, there is no bathing.
Vin_1.224. A hall is constructed for that purpose.
Vin_1.225: To wash robes without hope [of them being ruined], one may dig a pit lined with bricks.
Vin_1.226: This is the release from the water-vortex [of the offense].
Vin_1.227: When the remaining water is excessively hot, one should announce it [to the monks].
Vin_1.228 / Its breaking occurs due to cold. Vin_1.229 / Sprinkling and so forth [also cause it].
Vin_1.230 / The placing of a bowl filled with gravel, cow dung, and tooth-sticks [is prescribed].
Vin_1.231. If there is forbearance, one should not perform the *purobhaktika* (pre-meal) rite.
Vin_1.232. If someone approaches by way of the middle [path] and is unknown, one who has arrived here should question him for the purpose of ascertaining his identity.
Vin_1.233. This is the reason for stationing a gatekeeper.
Vin_1.234. And for the purpose of preventing entry by a monk;
Vin_1.235. one should not grant entry here to one who lacks faith;
Vin_1.236. the performance of service here is to be done together with the co-residents and pupils.
"By novices," says another [teacher].

[The duties consist of] providing lamps, cauldrons, oil, tooth-sticks, cow-dung, clay, powder, water, and so forth; as well as looking after the wood, massaging, anointing, bathing, sweeping, and clearing away refuse.
Vin_1.239: [The cleaning] of those [utensils] is done by one another.
Vin_1.240: Having ensured the cleanliness of the stools and the spittoons, they should be placed back in their proper places.
Vin_1.241: This is the rule for all such vessels; one should keep all equipment well-guarded and well-secured.
Vin_1.242: One should enter making little noise.
Vin_1.243: One should be pleasing to behold.
Vin_1.244: One who is well-restrained.
Vin_1.245 / Being fully aware.
Vin_1.246 / One should not fan [oneself] while standing in front [of others].
Vin_1.247 / Avoiding socializing in groups.
Vin_1.248: Noble one, maintaining silence is the support.

Vin_2.1690: Not [the robe] of one who has not cut [it]. Vin_2.1691: One should not wear a garment dyed with a primary color. Vin_2.1692: Not [the robe] of a householder.
One should share within the monastery the *kāṣāya* robe of one who has died; on the road, there is common ownership of a robe requested for wear;
[this applies] with fellow monks and novices who provide assistance.
Vin_2.1696. When there is only one person, [the robe] should be given from the end of the seniority list up to the point where it is deemed sufficient.
Vin_2.1697. One should not walk about in the walking-meditation hall (caṅkrama) wearing a robe that is not cut to size or that hangs down from below.
Vin_2.1698. If invited, one who desires merit may step forward after having struck [the robe] with the thought of impermanence, provided it is a new robe that has not yet had its fringes cut.
The use of unstained clothing;
(Vin_2,4,58) regarding the category of stimulating objects; in the case of touching and not touching, the agent is the jewel, which is not one's own property. (Vin_2.1699 [28b5])
And that which is approved by them;
this is a weapon belonging to the sphere of battle, and it is an implement belonging to the sphere of the Gandharvas;
its fitness for use has been attained through the root [of the ritual].
Vin_2.1703: It is a duṣkṛta offense if it is not obtained.

Vin_2.1704: Except for the acceptance [of ownership], it pertains to the monastery and its appurtenances when one has a mind that does not intend the destruction of the substance. Vin_2.1705: One should not neglect that.
Vin_2.1706: When departing after seven or eight days in this vicinity, one should cover [the area] with dust or with fragments of pottery. Vin_2.1707:
One should not give [something] to those who have not formed the intention [to receive it], even if they say, "I am the owner."
Vin_2.1708: If [the Sangha] does not arrive, one may deposit it in the treasury of the Sangha.

Vin_2.1709: One may keep it for a period up to six months. Vin_2.1710: After that, if [the Sangha] has not arrived, whatever acquisition is obtained on the ground for the Buddha or the Sangha, its utilization shall take place there.
Vin_2.1711. If [the object] is unsuitable, one should purchase it; if it is suitable, [one may take] immovable property from him.
Vin_2.1712. If the owner should arrive at that time, they should invite his permission and, if he desires, give [it back].
Vin_2.1713. If he should seek interest, they should say: "You do not value this highly enough, which was protected by us."
Vin_2.1714: When gems and the like are cut and polished, they possess suitability [for use].
Vin_2.1715: And when they are fashioned into bracelets, armlets, *kejurahāra*, necklaces, half-necklaces, or strings of pearls.
Vin_2.1716: When lutes, flutes, *vallarī* lutes, *mahatī* lutes, and *utghoṣaka* instruments are provided with strings.

Vin_2.1717: When there is the sounding of conch shells, kettledrums, tabors, and drums; Vin_2.1718: when a bow is strung; Vin_1719: when there is the true state [of the sound], or when there is the holding of a sword, a spear, or a javelin by one who possesses moral discipline.
Vin_2.1720: [This applies] to arrows, iron shafts, and half-iron shafts when they possess a barb;
Vin_2.1721: [and] to an image when it contains relics;
Vin_2.1722: having established the perception of the Teacher toward its sound.
Vin_2.1723: Glass beads, pearls, straw mats, bamboo stalks, woven mats, floor coverings, *maḍuka* pillows, *piñjanaka* pillows, and wooden blocks are worth half [the value of the standard].
Vin_2.1724: A lump of gold is considered unfit [for such valuation].
Vin_2.1725: Having hidden it out of fear, or having taken it away without causing obstruction—whether it belongs to oneself, to the Saṅgha, or to a stūpa—one may depart with that silver and gold.
Vin_2.1726 / By a faithful person or by a novice monk (śrāmaṇera).
Vin_2.1727 / In the absence [of such], by oneself.
Vin_2.1728 / Digging is what is meant here.
Vin_2.1729: [It is] a gift when [the recipient] has departed.
Vin_2.1730: Likewise, having uprooted [it].
Vin_2.1731: It is faultless in a non-human abode if their ground, buildings, and so forth are produced from merit and consist of jewels.

Vin_2.1732 / And when there is no other vessel available for food, one may set it down. Vin_2.1733 / And when sitting, one may set down the bedding and seating. Vin_2.1734 / One may travel by means of a vehicle.
Vin_2.1736 / Not [should one sit] with a haughty air. Vin_2.1737 / No one other than those who are aged or ill [should sit].
Vin_2.1738 / One may sit upon a jeweled lion-throne for the purpose of hearing the Dharma, having struck it down with the mental application of impermanence.
Vin_2.1739 / And regarding the phrase "in a dwelling belonging to householders," it refers to the designation [of such a place].
Vin_2.1740 / Regarding garments covered with golden-encrusted rings;
Vin_2.1741 / and here, regarding those inlaid with jewels and encrusted with gold and silver.
These should be introduced.

For those who have established the perception of the Teacher [in the recipient], even if there is no layperson or novice present, they may touch [the items] because of the nature of the Buddha and for the sake of the Dharma and its purpose;
and so too with that substance.
One should not resort to the wearing of ornaments. One should wear a seal-ring. It should be one that is not worn as a cloak.
Vin_2.1747: [A seal] may be made of tin, copper, lead, lac, wood, stone, clay, ivory, or horn.
Vin_2.1748: On a communal property, the mark in the center is a wheel, with two deer on the sides; below it, the name of the owner of the monastery. Vin_2.1749:
On a private property, it is a skeleton or a skull.
Vin_2.1750: One should not adorn the head with a *phaṇikā* (a type of head-ornament).
Vin_2.1751: This is an illustrative example.
Vin_2.1752: One should not look at one's face in a mirror.
Vin_2.1753 / [It is permissible] from water.
Vin_2.1754 / There is no offense if it is for the purpose of examining the water; nor if one sees a wound, wrinkles, or gray hair, provided one has grasped the preceding and subsequent signs.
Vin_2.1755 / One should not associate with one who has passed three years [of seniority].
Vin_2.1756. One should not apply ointments or anoint [the body]. Vin_2.1757. Nor should one use perfumes.
Vin_2.1758. However, those seeking merit may offer perfumes and unguents at the feet.
One should not bring [the bowl] before him; one who has not been ordained by these [precepts] should not join the Saṃgha;
and one should not teach the Dharma to householders.
Vin_2.1762 / One should not visit families.
Vin_2.1763 / One should bathe at the end [of the period]. Vin_2.1764 / One should accept [the robe] by name.
Vin_2.1765 / And flower garlands;
Vin_2.1766 / their application to caityas; Vin_2.1767 / even for a disciple.
Vin_2.1768: It is not intended [to be placed] at the head or at the feet of the donor.
Vin_2.1769: Not in front of the door.
Vin_2.1770: Not against the wall.

Vin_2.1772: One should smell it from time to time, thinking, "It is pleasing to the eye and fragrant.
Vin_2.1773: One should not resort to wearing the sacred thread (*brahmasūtra*).
Vin_2.1774: Not [to throw] a thread.
Vin_2.1775: One may apply a root-remedy for the purpose of treatment on the left side.
Vin_2.1776: One must not discard it anywhere at all.
If there is a remnant, it should be tied to the corner or the fold of the robe;
if not, it should be placed in a hole in a pillar or against a wall.
Vin_2.1779: One should not engage in dancing, singing, or instrumental music. Vin_2.1780: One should not teach them. Vin_2.1781: One should not provide them.
Vin_2.1782. One should not approach for the sake of seeing [a performance].
Vin_2.1783. One should not cause a nun to perform a dance.
Vin_2.1784. One should maintain the concealment of one's voice when praising the virtues of the Teacher or when reciting the Tridaṇḍaka.
One should train in this in a secluded place.
One should not engage in leaping, playing, shouting, frivolity, running about, or physical striking.
One should not distort one’s body or speech with the intention of being frivolous.
Vin_2.1788 / Mixing [food] by portions constitutes a *saṃsarga* offense.
Vin_2.1789 / One should not consume food using a vessel-circulator.
Vin_2.1790 / One should not string together a flower-ornament.
Vin_2.1791 / One should not release [the student].
Vin_2.1792 / One should not grant [instruction] by merely looking at the forehead.
Vin_2.1793 / One should not teach while remaining in a state of equanimity.
One should not perform jumping or leaping.
One should not turn over one's thighs, arms, or fish-like body.
One should not pierce a water-sieve.

One should not play water-frogs or *bherika* drums. One should not splash water with a ladle. One should not imitate the trumpeting of elephants, the neighing of horses, the bellowing of bulls, or the cries of peacocks and cuckoos.
One must not play mouth-trumpets, ḍuḍḍukas, or kettledrums;
this pertains to matters that cause excessive excitement.
(Vin_2,4,59) Regarding bathing:
(Vin_2.1801) From the middle of the summer until one and a half months before the rains;

Vin_2.1803 / By the wind that has not been stirred up;

One should consider that this [offense] does not exist among the Aparāntakas;
one should not rely on the opinion of another regarding its occurrence, for it is a *snāta-prāyaścittika*.

**(Vin_2,4,61)** Regarding the instilling of remorse: *Vin_2.1818*—when one instills remorse in a monk for the sake of [causing him] regret by saying, "You have not been fully ordained," or "You have committed a defeat (pārājika)," and so forth; *Vin_2.1819*—this constitutes an offense for the monk [if done] with a mind intended to produce discomfort.
Vin_2.1820: Even by way of jest;
Vin_2.1821: even when there is no arising;
Vin_2.1822: of remorse.
If another person commits an offense,
it constitutes a *duṣkṛta* (wrongdoing) for one who instills remorse in them.

(Vin_2,4,62) Regarding prodding: (Vin_2.1824) for a monk, (Vin_2.1825) if he touches [another] with his fingers, fist, jewel, shoulder, head, side, back, hip, thigh, calf, knee, or big toe, etc., while intending to scatter [the other], [he commits an offense].

Therefore, there is an offense by seeing [marks such as] scars, moles, sesame-seed spots, or the curling of body hair. Some say that it is an offense for one who, having seen many [such marks], reports them as one. [This constitutes] a *pratideśanīya* (confession) offense.
(Vin_2,4,64) In the case of causing excitement by means of fluids; (Vin_2.1828) in the performance of activities related to water;

(Vin_2.1829) for one who has entered [the water], [this refers to] diving and surfacing, moving back and forth between the banks, exertion against the current, playing with water-drums, hand-drums, and lutes, piercing with a looped net, performing circular movements, making diamond-patterns, well-pits, whirlpools, and drawing lines.
The primary [offense] for those who cause [water] to flow away;
a *duṣkṛta* for taking *ṛṭipyaka*;
[the same applies to taking] a water-pot, a watering-can, or a shallow bowl.
Vin_2.1832: And in the case of gruel, soup, broth, and cream, even though they are indeed hot;
Vin_2.1833: and in the case of causing laughter that is not [intended as] sport;
Vin_2.1834: likewise, it is the cause for that which has become such.
Vin_2.1835: [It is] by means of the desire to experience the antidote to restlessness and zeal.
Vin_2.1836: Therefore, there is no offense when one enters [the water] with the desire for refreshment.
Vin_2.1837: In the training regarding swimming, [it is permitted] whether one swims crosswise or lengthwise.
When one draws lines on heated surfaces with the desire to lick them,
it constitutes the offense of causing moisture and excitement.
(Vin_2,4,65) Regarding sleeping with a woman:
Vin_2.1839 / When one falls asleep during the night in the same dwelling together with a female person (mātṛgrāma). Vin_2.1840 / This constitutes an offense of the *antika* class.
Vin_2.1841: Previously, it was a duṣkṛta.
Vin_2.1842: Having made this [measure] the size of a hen, [it is] within;
[this is] sleeping together with a woman.
(Vin_2,4,66) Regarding "terrifying": (Vin_2.1843) even by means of a look of laughter, with the intention of terrifying, preceded by the presentation of a cause for fear;
(Vin_2.1844) [this refers to] the case where, even if another person does not actually produce fear in a monk by saying, "Such-and-such a terrifying being is Yama."
The fundamental [offense] regarding that which is unpleasant:

for example, the appearance of those known as *preta*, *piśāca*, *kumbhāṇḍa*, *kaṭapūtana*, and *tārkṣya*; or the forms of insects, of small insects, of charcoal, and of burnt pillars; or the sounds of lions, tigers, leopards, owls, *paṭara*, *rubhra*, and *ṛkṣa*.
Vin_2.1848: [The offense of] excrement, urine, mud, or filth;
Vin_2.1849: [The offense of] contact with *kiṭaka*, *kiṃlaṃjaka*, or *kutapa*; Vin_2.1850:
For that which is pleasing to the mind, it is a *duṣkṛta*.
Namely: those that manifest the forms of gods, nāgas, gandharvas, yakṣas, kinnaras, and mahoragas;
the sounds of lutes and other instruments; and the fragrances of agallochum, sandalwood, saffron, and tamāla leaves.
[This refers to] the touch of fine silk, cotton cloth, woolen garments, *dukūla*, and *koṭṭamvaka*. [The rule concerns] the purpose of abandoning [attachment to] such things.
Therefore, there is no offense in speaking about the hells, animals, hungry ghosts, and humans for the sake of inducing spiritual urgency (*saṃvega*).
Terrifying.
(Vin_2,4,67) Regarding concealment:

Vin_2.1858. This refers to the depositing of the requisites for the livelihood of a recluse—such as the bowl, robes, water-strainer, bronze vessel, waist-band, and so forth—which belong to one who has gone forth.
And in causing [something] to be deposited; with the desire for what has been relinquished to be beneficial;
[and] the act of guarding.
(Vin_2,4,68) Regarding one who lives on what has been given:
(Vin_2.1861) It is an offense for a monk to use a robe that has been given to him without its permission being granted;
(Vin_2.1862) provided that there is no expectation of pleasure arising from that cause.
One who lives on what has been given.
(Vin_2,4,69) Regarding "ill-spoken":
(Vin_2.1863) When a monk, with the intent to disparage, makes a formal declaration while misapprehending the offense that constitutes a *saṃghāvaśeṣa*,
it is an offense of expiation for ill-spoken words (*asvākhyāna-prāyaścittika*).
(Vin_2,4,70) Regarding traveling with women: Vin_2.1865 / [Traveling] out of desire on a vehicle drawn by animals;
Vin_2.1866 / [Traveling] against the current.
Vin_2.1867: Half of that [measure] constitutes a *duṣkṛta* offense.
Vin_2.1868: [The same applies to] one who causes [the caravan] to travel beyond the limit of a journey.
Vin_2.1869: [The same applies to] one who causes a lost person to descend from the road onto the path.
Or, for one who is unable to carry [the burden],
traveling together with a woman.
(Vin_2,4,71) Regarding traveling together with thieves:
(Vin_2.1871) With village-robbers, thieves, or merchants who evade customs duties;
(Vin_2.1872) with fraudulent practitioners or those who have gone forth as thieves—it is a *duṣkṛta* offense.
Accompanying one who commits theft. **(Vin_2,4,72)** Regarding ordination when [the candidate] is deficient:
**Vin_2.1873** [this refers to] conferring full ordination upon one who is less than twenty years of age.
Vin_2.1874 / Regarding the conferring of full ordination with one as the preceptor:
Vin_2.1875 / He [the preceptor] must not fail to ask him about his completeness; Vin_2.1876 / nor may others [fail to do so].
Vin_2.1877: They should not confer full ordination (*upasaṃpadā*) upon her without having ascertained this.
Vin_2.1878: In every case, the established rule for conferring full ordination is for one who has completed twenty years [of age].
Vin_2.1879: For the other [case], it is when there is the perception that she has completed [the required age].
And in cases of forgetfulness, doubt, or uncertainty;
and in the case of knowledge, there is the destruction [of the offense]. This is not so, however, if it has been previously attained.
Even if [the age] is increased by the months spent in the womb, it is a deficient ordination if it is less than half [a year].
(Vin_2,4,73) Regarding the excavation of the ground:
Vin_2.1884; regarding digging and causing to dig:
Vin_2.1885; regarding earth and soil.

Vin_2.1886: Except for the case of a novice builder who, while engaged in the practice of astrology, drives in a wooden peg measuring four finger-breadths because a preparer of the site is not present. Vin_2.1887:
If it is [done] intentionally, it is a *maula* offense; Vin_2.1888: if not, it is a *duṣkṛta*.
The first [case] is when one has stayed for three months without forming a group.
If it is a wilderness region of rain, [the limit is] six [months]; otherwise, it is six [days].
One should not think that [the effect] did not exist previously in the throat; rather,
the causal efficacy of moments resides in the collection as a whole.
Therefore, it is entirely [lost] when she has been chosen elsewhere;
[it is lost] when she is missing or burnt;
[and there is] half [the value] for one who is missing.
And [it applies] to crumbling earth, earthen crusts, riverbanks, rags, and plaster coatings; and also when there is an excess of gravel, sand, and so forth; and [it applies] to actions.
Vin_2.1901: This applies to one whose intention is to cause confusion.
Vin_2.1902: Therefore, there is no offense for one whose intention is merely to count, to set down [the items], and so forth.
[This concludes] the section on the displacement of the ground.
(Regarding the offense of over-indulgence after having been invited:
