Vin_5.53 / When [the boundary] has been raised and there is no one authorized [to maintain it], the limit is within the boundary of the *araṇya*.
Vin_5.54 / Upon its interruption, there is inclusion within that circle (*maṇḍala*). Vin_5.55 / With reference to this, here [it is said]:
Vin_5.56: Its completion occurs upon crossing the boundary.
Vin_5.57: It occurs with the intention of not returning.
Vin_5.58: And its arising occurs outside the boundary.

Vin_5.59: In the absence [of the robe], if there is a continuous intention to make a robe, that very [period] applies. Vin_5.60: If the intention to make it ceases while it is still to be made, [the period] exists. Vin_5.61: It is completed when [the robe] has been obtained.

Vin_5.62. For one who is about to perform [the formal act] among the three, this is the configuration: when the hope for completion is cut off, there is the destruction of what was begun; thus it is the conclusion. Vin_5.63. There is doubt, as in the case of the determination of the remover. Vin_5.64.
They should not persist in making a disparaging gesture toward the ritual action.
Vin_5.65 / The time for that is the month of Phālguna. Vin_5.66 / During the interval.
Vin_5.67 / Even if it is earlier, provided there is the intent to steal.
Vin_5.68: Because it is heard, even when not personally experienced, there is a subsequent conformity toward that [object] which constitutes a benefit.
Vin_5.69: Because it is woven through non-existent entities.
Vin_5.70: Because of the cutting off [of the continuum], it is considered [to be present].
Vin_5.71: One should not distribute the temporary gains of all [the monks] until [the kaṭhina] has been formally removed. // The Chapter on the Kaṭhina // 1 //
(Vin_5,2) Pertaining to the inquiry; Vin_5.72:
The spreading [of the robe] according to the invitation; Vin_5.73:
Not at the end of the *upoṣadha*.
Vin_5.74 / And there is the removal; Vin_5.75 / its [status] is that of the same day;
Vin_5.76 / furthermore, the state of being removed occurs when the Poṣadha has been performed.
Vin_5.77. Having spread it separately, there is success when [the community] is divided.
Vin_5.78. He is the one who spreads it among those who speak according to the Dharma.
Vin_5.79. Even when this has been done, their entitlement to the gains in the residence remains intact for the others.

Vin_5.80. There shall be no rising up from the dwelling of those who have been suspended (*utkṣiptaka*) for those who are in their natural state (*prakṛtisthaka*). Vin_5.81. "Being" (*bhāva*) refers to the act of sitting down; it is the taking of a seat. Vin_5.82. Through the power of granting one's consent (*chanda*), there is the status of "it being done" when that which is to be performed by a group has been completed by the remaining members.
Vin_5.83. That [act] is the non-falling away; it is the lifting up. Vin_5.84.
Therefore, if one has not given consent, there is no rising from sleep or meditative attainment, nor is there a lifting up of the matting, prior to hearing [the proclamation].
Vin_5.85. Regarding the state of having dwelt within a single boundary, for those who have dwelt in other residences therein, [the rule applies] to the matting.
Vin_5.86. Its status as "that place" shall exist at the time of the formal spreading [of the robe].
Vin_5.87. And its status as "that place" exists when, having spread it, a separate boundary is established for it.
Vin_5.88. If these are distinct for each monastery, their removal [from the formal spreading] shall take place separately.
Vin_5.89 / [The offense occurs] when there is a breach of the counter-measure.
Vin_5.90 / There is no non-removal if the removal of the *anāstāra* has not been performed.
Vin_5.91 / There is no failure to fulfill [the requirement] because of the absence of rising [to perform the service].
Vin_5.92: Because it was spread out in various places, there is no offense in its removal. Vin_5.93: There is no fault for one who has formally spread the kaṭhina.
Vin_5.94: Even without his outer robe (saṃghāṭī), he may enter a village and so forth, provided he sits down at a crossroads.
// The section on questions concerning the *kaṭhina* robe-material // 2 //
And the section on the Kaṭhina is completed. 5.
*Vinaya* 6, Chapter on Robes / (Vin_6.1) Chapter on Robes / Vin_6.1:
One should not use a garment that has not been cut with a blade.
Vin_6.2: One should resolve upon a robe that has been cut and sewn for the purpose of being a *cīvara*.
Vin_6.3: It should be free from variegated patterns, with its borders even and its middle uniform, and it should be adorned with the appropriate leaf-patterns and edges.
Vin_6.4: [The three robes are] the inner garment (*antaravāsa*), the upper garment (*uttarāsaṅga*), and the outer cloak (*saṃghāṭī*).
Vin_6.5: [The same applies] regarding a small storehouse and a communal robe for the Saṅgha, as well as for a nun of that same kind.
Vin_6.6: Even when there is a possibility of death, [one may accept] through a formal request.
Vin_6.7: One should not cause this to reach the ears of those who dwell in the monastery.
Vin_6.8. If another [robe] is not available, one may perform the formal act of authorization (*adhiṣṭhāna*) for a robe that is not dyed.
Vin_6.9. And also for one that has not been cut.
Vin_6.10. In this case, if it is possible, there should be the giving of patches (*āsevakā*).
Vin_6.11 And [it applies to] that which belongs to a householder.
Vin_6.12 [This includes] felt, woolen cloth, blankets, thick woolens, and *pailātika* cloth, provided they are uncut, made from the wool of sheep that have not yet been shorn.
Vin_6.13 At that very moment, upon obtaining it, one should clean the bedding and furniture from impurities.

Vin_6.14: One should not use communal bedding—whether a couch, a bed, or a stool—that is not covered with a spread, nor should one use it by giving a covering or concealing it with the intention [of using it].
Vin_6.15: And all that is variegated is destroyed if used more than once.
Vin_6.16: Nor [should one use it] when it has become unsuitable or when it is soiled.
Vin_6.17 / Regarding the storage of a spreader-cloth (*pratyāstaraṇa*), that which is single-layered is permissible. Vin_6.18 / That which is double-layered is made of *pailotika* cloth.
Vin_6.19 / That which is variegated with various patterns is not allowable.
Vin_6.20. One should fashion its opening like that of a bird's beak.
Vin_6.21. [The opening] should be at the lower third or similar portion. Vin_6.22. One should not rely upon it if it consists of a single piece.
Vin_6.23. One who has it should carry a covering for itching.
Vin_6.24. He should wash it with the five kinds of alkaline substances. Vin_6.25. Silk, wool, hemp, and linen are permitted.
Vin_6.26 / It should not be worn with the ends hanging down. Vin_6.27 / Taking up [the practice] of wearing hair, fire, or owl-wings.
Vin_6.28 / This is a gross [offense].
Vin_6.29 / This is another [type of] vessel.

Vin_6.30 / [The following are forbidden: pulling out the hair, leaf-cloths, skins used as inner or upper garments, the *yāpana*, the *tiriṭa*, the *aṅganāḍī*, the prohibition against all-blue [robes], robes with long borders, the *phaṇa-daśaka*, the *kañcuka*, the turban (*uṣṇīṣa*), head-wraps, straw mats (*kutapa*), bricks, and the banners of the various non-Buddhist sects (*tīrthika*).
Vin_6.31. Even by means of a mere measure of cotton-seed, leaf-filling, or lamp-wick, there is an equal distribution.
Vin_6.32. Having sold it, [the distribution] is according to that regulation. Vin_6.33. Not by tearing it apart.
Vin_6.34: "The distribution of the five [types of] acquisitions shall take place; today the acquisition will be distributed. You must assemble there"—this is the announcement to the Saṃgha.
Vin_6.35: The striking of the *gaṇḍī*. Vin_6.36: The distribution of the voting sticks (*śalākā*).
Vin_6.37 / Counting; Vin_6.38 / Invitation by individual allotment;
Vin_6.40 / Not when it has not been concluded.
Vin_6.41. This also applies to the acquisition of a family.
Vin_6.42. One who is ineligible does not [gain a share] when the distribution of that acquisition has already begun.
Vin_6.43. Therefore, one should appoint [an agent] while departing for the purpose of receiving it.
Vin_6.44: [It is an offense] for one who has promised to become a bandit when not actually seized.
Vin_6.45: [An offense] regarding family gains starting from five *paṇas*.
Vin_6.46: One should not accept [a gift] unless it has been announced.
Vin_6.47 / The preceptor or the teacher may accept it.
Vin_6.48 / And for the sake of a place of trust.
Vin_6.49 / Not for the sake of one's own faction.
Vin_6.50. This also applies to bedding and seating. Vin_6.51. Or to food.
Vin_6.52. When taking for the sake of another, one should inform them.
Vin_6.53. There is no [valid] separation by entering into that [community].
Vin_6.54. Unity does not exist for one who is half-way; and being unworthy (*asuvarṇatā*) is the reason for the non-attainment [of the goal] when one who is unworthy enters.
Vin_6.55. One who is unworthy of the gains of the Saṃgha is one who has fallen into the faction of unrighteousness among those who are divided.

Vin_6.56. Regarding the state of having dwelt for a longer time: when there is a gain at that specific time, it applies to one who has already resided there, provided there is no loss of that gain and no departure, even upon death. Vin_6.57. The determination of the distribution of gains is according to the specific regulations.
Vin_6.58. And it is also determined by those who receive the gains.
Vin_6.59: Even when the instruction is given in its entirety;
Vin_6.60: When the boundary of the community has not been delimited by the ritual boundary, there is a delimitation [of it]; Vin_6.61: In this case, the reality [of the number] is one and so forth.
Vin_6.62. Regarding the acquisition of Dharma, the reciters thereof have ownership over it.
Vin_6.63. Retaining even a single verse of a seer constitutes the limit in terms of reality.
Vin_6.64. Arhatship [is attained] by one whose gender has changed in the presence of others, regarding the requisites of the deceased.
Vin_6.65. Likewise for one who has been suspended.
Vin_6.66. Or when he is not present, [the offense ceases] once the motive has ceased in his mind.
Vin_6.67. There is no breach of this [vow] regarding the state of being perceived by the stars and so forth.
Vin_6.68: [The offense] belongs to one who has caused a schism in a schismatic community.

Vin_6.69: No one other than a fellow-celibate (sabrahmacārin) who has gone forth possesses authority over that [schism]. Vin_6.70: It does not apply to one who has been authorized by a formal motion (jñapti), nor to one who has attained it through prior or subsequent action.
Vin_6.71: For someone [who has died], there is the giving [of their belongings] to the senior and junior members of the Saṃgha; that is what is designated by that term. Vin_6.72:
Wherever the one who was to be authorized has gone, those within that boundary possess the authority to authorize.
Vin_6.73: In this context, "not performing" refers to being in a state of death.

Vin_6.74. For those who have gone from within the boundary to a place outside the boundary, whether their bodies are touching the ground or otherwise, their transgression occurs as soon as they have reached that [outside] location.

Vin_6.75. When there is a corresponding object, the requisites belong to the one who is at that [location]. Vin_6.76. They may, by means of the corresponding object, formally authorize [the requisites] for another who is standing elsewhere.

Vin_6.77. When that which has been sent is not rejected, ownership of it arises through the act of giving. Vin_6.78. When it is rejected, the status of being the sender remains with the one who sent it.
Vin_6.79. Even in the case of what was rejected, [ownership] belongs to that [sender].
Vin_6.80: Its establishment is outside of this [boundary].
Vin_6.81: Within the boundary, it is established solely by one who possesses the designation [of a monk].
Vin_6.82: They should not establish [the boundary] unless there has been the removal [of obstacles], the honoring [of the site], the hearing of the Dharma, and the instruction on the fee (dakṣiṇā).

Vin_6.83. When staying inside a house, the ownership of the bowl and robe belongs to whichever householder gives them as a gift. Vin_6.84. If [the recipient] is an Arhat, Vin_6.85. and he has lost [them], then by him [they are forfeited].
Vin_6.86: [The offense occurs] when one does not give to someone who has requested it.
Vin_6.87: [The offense occurs] in the sequence, first. Vin_6.88:
[The offense occurs] when, because there is no sentient being and thus no instruction, one has gone after being asked.
Vin_6.89: Likewise in the case of succession.
Vin_6.90: That which arises from a debt belongs to the one to whom the measure of what was to be given belongs; this applies to the estate of one who has died.
Vin_6.91: This also applies to that which has been divided.
Vin_6.92: That which was deposited together with him may be given to him or received from him, but not by him alone.
Vin_6.93: By this, fellow-practitioners (sabrahmacārin) do not incur a debt.

Vin_6.94: Regarding the illumination of jewels, as many as are required for that purpose, they are not to be employed by a novice; rather, they are to be used equally for the attendant of the sick and for those who go there, as part of the six types of requisites.
There is no state of being subject to empowerment.
(Vin 6.95) It belongs to the middle [person] with respect to the superior and the inferior.
(Vin 6.96) Its commonality exists when there is multiplicity.

Vin_6.97. When the sick person has departed and died, the property must be given for that specific purpose. Vin_6.98. This does not apply to the property of one who has died while being unworthy. Vin_6.99. Nor does it apply when he has passed away elsewhere.
Vin_6.100: In this case, full arhatship is not attained.
Vin_6.101: For one who is ill, there is a loss [of property] according to what has been stated regarding giving; as it was stated regarding giving, so must the duty be performed.
Vin_6.102: There is no passing away [of ownership] for the owner when the property is made his own at the time of death.
Vin_6.103: Departure for a householder. Vin_6.104: Having handed over the wife to the son, when she has died, acting as one pleases regarding her son and wife.
Vin_6.105: Handing over the elephants, horses, camels, donkeys, mules, and their armor to the king.
Vin_6.106: Regarding the three [categories], there is [an offense] for gold and silver, whether wrought or unwrought.

Vin_6.107: And for gems. Vin_6.108: If that is otherwise, even if it is not deficient in value because it is a part of that [object], it is the same; however, this is not so in the case of pearls belonging to the Buddha.
Vin_6.109: And [the same applies] to a large stage.
Vin_6.110: Having ground the plaster, one should apply it to the fragrant wall.
Vin_6.111: That which is not for awakening should be employed for the ornaments of images, fragrant shrines, and reliquaries.
Vin_6.112: For the purpose of establishing the writing of the Buddha’s word, provided it is in accordance with the Dharma.
Vin_6.113: Regarding a vehicle, [it is permissible] for the sake of an image.
Vin_6.114: For the sake of a banner, [it is permissible] for those of that lineage.
Vin_6.115: And [the use] of staffs and those things suitable for them;
Vin_6.116: other weapons in the Saṃgha;
Vin_6.117: having made a rattle, a needle, or a small knife their refuge.

Vin_6.118. Regarding other property belonging to the Saṃgha that has been deposited: it is appropriate to assign the vessels, foods, fields, houses, shops, bedding, seats, utensils, iron goods, and the families of barbers, potters, and carpenters;
as well as water-cloths, containers, male and female slaves, laborers, servants, oxen, buffaloes, goats, sheep, medicines, and books of the Buddha’s teachings that are easy to produce or transcribe.
Among these, the first [category] is the most worthy.
Vin_6.119: [The storage of] cloth, woven garments, upper robes, woolen blankets, cotton, oil-jars, small pots, water-pots, books, writing materials, and pigments is permitted for a second [monk].
Vin_6.120: For a third [monk], there is permission for five measures of sesame, rice, barley, beans, and inferior grains, as well as food and drink.
[The Chapter on Robes, Part 1.]
(Vin_6,2) Included in the section on miscellaneous matters:
Vin_6.121. One should construct [the boundary] as a circle, a semicircle, or a partial circle. Vin_6.122. For the purpose of measurement, one should carry a staff of that same length.
And [the rule applies] to the openings of the bowls (Vin 6.123). (Vin 6.124) One should hold a measuring stick of that same dimension.
(Vin 6.125) Its maximum length is four finger-breadths.
Vin_6.126 / Or it may be a *vitasti* of a crow.
Vin_6.127 / In case of reduction, it is two and a half *aṅguṣṭhotkara*s.
Vin_6.128 / One should not spread out the robe on the ground.

Vin_6.129: The making of the *kaṭhina* for that purpose. Vin_6.130: It is made of wood or bamboo. Vin_6.131: It is square; it has a hole for the purpose of securing the binding and for the purpose of providing space for the thread; it is so named.
Vin_6.132: [He may keep] as many robes as there are.
Vin_6.133: He may cut [them] with a blade.
Vin_6.134: He should wear them.
Vin_6.135: It should be shaped like a crow’s beak or like a cock’s wing.
Vin_6.136: It must not be made of anything other than iron.
Vin_6.137: It must not have a handle that is polished, smooth, variegated, or highly decorated.
Vin_6.138: There is no [fixed] measurement for one that exceeds six finger-breadths.
Vin_6.139: Others say there is none for eight [finger-breadths].
Vin_6.140: There is no purpose in one that is less than four finger-breadths.
Vin_6.141: One should use it when it has been smeared with applied cow dung.
Vin_6.142: In the absence of cow dung, when it has been swept clean with ashes.
Vin_6.143: One should sew this [robe].
Vin_6.144: Even with a needle.
Vin_6.145: One should carry this.
Vin_6.146: Not one made of any other material than bronze, copper, brass, or clay.
Vin_6.147: There is another [rule]: [it applies] to those made of copper or iron, and to those that are sharp.
Vin_6.148: One should hold its handle, which may be ring-shaped, tubular, or fist-shaped.
Vin_6.149: One should not entrust this to a shameless person or a novice monk.
Vin_6.150. Needles, knives, and awls, when protected with honey and rice-dust, should be placed in a leather pouch for the purpose of preventing them from being lost.
Vin_6.151. To prevent the loss of dice, one should give a piece of cloth by attaching a fastener to the robe.
Vin_6.152. And the same applies to a knotted cord.
Vin_6.153. One should not have a dyed or undyed cloth washed by a washerman.
Vin_6.154. Nor should one do so oneself in that same manner.
Vin_6.155. Nor on a mat, nor on a wooden board or wall.
One should gradually warm a lake with lukewarm water according to its characteristics (Vin 6.157);
turning it over with both hands (Vin 6.158), or,
if unable to do so, with both feet.
Vin_6.159: It is permissible to console a householder in this manner.
Vin_6.160: One should protect him from changing his conduct. Vin_6.161: One should wear a rag-robe that has been well-washed and dyed.

Vin_6.162: One should not [wear] a robe stained with impurities. Vin_6.163: Drying [the robe] in shade or sunlight is for the sake of its proper condition, provided the dye has been thoroughly mixed. Vin_6.164: Except when traveling on a journey, one should not [go] without a robe.

Vin_6.165: Superiority up to the third [repetition]. Vin_6.166: Therefore, when there is a plurality [of repetitions], the taking up occurs three times. Vin_6.167: Inferiority on the part of the other.
Vin_6.168: Therefore, there should be a separate placement [of the bowl].
Vin_6.169: It consists of writing, beginning with the first [letter], and so forth.
Vin_6.170: And the first [letter] is to be used for the preceding [word].
Vin_6.171. And [this applies] to one whose robes have been stolen.
Vin_6.172. Having removed it from that [robe], he should give a piece of that same size to a *kuṇḍālaka* (a small bowl or vessel).
Vin_6.173. It is to be worn in a liquid.
Vin_6.174: [The rule applies] when the heartwood is completely dried out. Vin_6.175: Therefore, it applies to that which is of medium quality.
Vin_6.176: In a desolate region, thorough drying is required.
Vin_6.177: By means of moving about on hot coals or heated iron plates.
Vin_6.178: For those who are difficult to restrain, by designating the armpits as the place for punishment.
Vin_6.179: Repeatedly turning over the limbs with various side-ward torments.
Vin_6.180: It is proper to give new dyeing material for new robes. Vin_6.181: One should give old dyeing material for old robes.
Vin_6.182: New [dye] should be dried in the sun.
Vin_6.183: [The rule applies] in the shade of old [trees].
Vin_6.184: The giving of a water-pot for the purpose of providing non-sentient [water]. Vin_6.185: On the following day.
Vin_6.186. They shall not perform painting work on a clean walking path (caṅkrama). Vin_6.187. Nor in a monastery (vihāra). Vin_6.188.
Nor upon its roof.
Vin_6.189: Not within the vicinity of the rinsing-water vessel.
Vin_6.190: Giving [food] in a place that has been smeared [with impurity].
Vin_6.191: If it is pure and not smeared, there is no offense.
Vin_6.192: If wind and rain arrive while the construction of a palace is underway, it constitutes a formal act (*karaṇa*).
Vin_6.193: Once that area has been plastered, it constitutes a formal act.
Vin_6.194: [This is done] with cow dung or clay.
Vin_6.195. One should not partake of the use of a robe that has not been properly prepared through the ritual of *kalpa* and the subsequent *pratyākoṭita* (reversal) procedure.
In this context, "preparation" (*kalpa*) refers to the washing.
Regarding water, there is no requirement for it to be boiled.
When it is completely purified of dew, it is easier to fold the hand by half over the lower part of the body that has been clothed,
securing it with a strip,
a patch, a hook, or a toggle.

From a bundle of various ornaments, or from a dyer’s shop, one should take a thread of color; it should be similarly variegated. One should then lay down the robe upon a ground covered with various carpets.

Vin_6.196. Not in an impure place. Vin_6.197. When one has the strength to do so, one should not carry a burden while being stepped upon by a superior. Vin_6.198. One should not make use of what is intended for the use of another.
Vin_6.199. One should not use the *uttarāsaṅga* for cleaning oneself after voiding excrement or urine.
Vin_6.200. One should not sit upon it.

Vin_6.201. Except for the sake of wandering for alms, eating, paying homage at a caitya, performing acts of courtesy, attending an assembly of the Saṃgha, receiving instruction, or listening to the Dharma, one should not use the *saṃghāṭī* for any other activity.
Vin_6.202. One should not sit upon it, nor lie down upon it.
Vin_6.203. One should not step over it. Vin_6.204. One should not employ it for the sake of anyone at all.
Vin_6.205. One should not consume [food] by touching it with the body. Vin_6.206. By means of the "armpit-method," there is no perfection of the mouth in the right side of the face. Vin_6.207.
To prevent that from occurring, one should place a cloth over that region of the face.
Vin_6.208: [It shall be] one and a half cubits in width.
Vin_6.209: It shall be fastened on both sides with eight cords.
Vin_6.210: From time to time, it must be washed and dyed.
Vin_6.211. This [is made] with red ochre.
Vin_6.212. One should keep a face-cloth.
Vin_6.213. One whose body is sweating [should use] a body-rubbing cloth.
Vin_6.214. He should wear it over his inner robe.
Vin_6.215. If it becomes stuck [with impurities], he should soften it with decoction water mixed with soda, and then gently remove the pus and blood. Vin_6.216.
From time to time, he should wash, dry, and dye it.
Vin_6.217: This is proper for him by way of the [proper] element.
Vin_6.218: He should not leave his robes anywhere at random. Vin_6.219: For that purpose, he should arrange a bamboo rack.
Vin_6.220: For that purpose, [it is used] for a trough.
Vin_6.221: While the monastery is being constructed. Vin_6.222: Once it is completed, there is no further breach.
Vin_6.223. This illustration applies to both a monastery and a communal dwelling.
Vin_6.224. There is the successful acquisition of a creeper and a cord for this.
Vin_6.225. It is proper to carry garments by means of a small carrying-net.
Vin_6.226: One should perform this.
Vin_6.227: Having doubled the service [of the cloth] to two and a half handspans.
Vin_6.228: Making an opening in the middle.
Vin_6.229: Here, the net should be given without a cord.
Vin_6.230: It should be fastened by another [means]. Vin_6.231: It should be placed above those things being used.
Vin_6.232: Having looked [back], if one intends to depart on the following day; Vin_6.233: One should go only after having obtained permission from one's teachers;
Vin_6.234: Having performed the sprinkling of one’s own dwelling and other such duties.

Vin_6.235. One should travel on the road either with a discourse on the Dharma or in noble silence. Vin_6.236. At a place of rest, one may recite a verse or a proverb. Vin_6.237. And also when taking water for drinking.
Vin_6.238: [It is] for the sake of that person to whom that water belongs.
Vin_6.239: And for another deity.
Vin_6.240: A triple-staffed staff for the sake of clothing.
Vin_6.241. One should carry it in a small bag.
Vin_6.242. Its size should be from one hundred and fifty hand-spans up to one hundred hand-spans.
Vin_6.243. According to another [opinion], it should be in accordance with the local custom.

Vin_6.244. One should not go among householders in a place where water is difficult to obtain without this [practice]. Vin_6.245. Having shaken out one's robes, having hoisted them on a flagpole, having bathed, having washed one's hands and feet, or having taken up water and rinsed one's mouth, and having put on the three robes, one should enter the monastery with a peaceful deportment.

Vin_6.246: Having paid homage to the four elders, one should remain standing. Vin_6.247: In an ordinary place, one should be free from noise. Vin_6.248: One who is pleasing and well-restrained should counteract [the fault] with his majestic presence.
Vin_6.249: One should not allow a fellow student (*satīrthya*) to remain if he is not recognized [as such].
Vin_6.250: "Close the door; do not give [anything]; he is searching for [something] and must be turned away.

Regarding one who has been sent back, [the rule applies] to one who accepts [the gift], to one who has neglected [to turn him away], to one who has brought [the gift] while being offered as an object of trust, and to one who thinks, "This is my companion," and so forth.
Servitude arises through the act of offering oneself.
(Vin 6.251) Relying on a token of recognition is the means for one who is unknown to attain a specific status through another.
(Vin 6.252) If, at the end, there is a closing of the eyes while being presented [with the gift], [the transaction is not valid].

Vin_6.253: The performance [of the formal act] for the sake of ensuring that the question is not neglected or left incomplete. Vin_6.254: In the case of loss, when what was requested is not obtained due to impurity or because of failure [to provide it], there is the payment of the price for the taking of the mind [of the recipient], as well as the receiving of the bowl and the robes.
Vin_6.256: The preparation of a seat. Vin_6.257: An invitation to wash the feet. Vin_6.258: And with water.
Vin_6.259: Paying homage; Vin_6.260: Inquiring after one’s well-being;
Vin_6.261: Acting in a way that causes affection according to one's ability.
Vin_6.262: He should provide suitable bedding and seating.
Vin_6.263: He should approach the senior of the Saṃgha.
Vin_6.264: When receiving dependence, he should do so if that person appoints him.
Vin_6.265. If he is senior, he should appoint someone to distribute this bedding and seating.
Vin_6.266. He should not request bedding and seating impulsively.
Vin_6.267. Regarding the distribution of the tiers of seats: for a torn robe, there is a repair; its collection is done with patches.

Vin_6.268. Having left [the robe] to soak in the open air for seven or eight days above a tree or similar object, and having washed it after five or six days have passed, one may use the *śavacīvara*.

Vin_6.269. When invited with the announcement, "I am a cemetery-dweller (*śmaśānika*)," one who has not relinquished his claim of ownership may enjoy entry into both the monastery and the household, as well as their use; however, he must not use the bedding or seating belonging to the Saṃgha.
Vin_6.270. He must not use the bedding or seating belonging to the Saṃgha.
Vin_6.271. One should avoid circumambulating a *caitya* within a distance of one *vyāma*.
Vin_6.272. One should carry a mosquito net.
Vin_6.273. [It may be made of] wool, hemp, cotton, *natuka*, or leaf-buds.
Vin_6.274: It shall not be made of elephant, horse, cow, hair, or similar materials.
Vin_6.275: In all cases, it must be polished and smooth; it may be variegated or multi-colored, provided it is not decorated with the likeness of a teacher or a śalika bird.
Vin_6.276: And there shall be a mosquito net.
Vin_6.277: [It is permissible] to sew it from above with a patch.
Vin_6.278: By binding it to a stick.
Vin_6.279: Of one measuring four cubits.
Vin_6.280. Covering with a cloth twelve cubits in length. Vin_6.281. With support.
Vin_6.282. Then there is support for his bedding and seating.
Vin_6.283: The making of a door-bolt for a door. Vin_6.284: Fanning is a remedy against heat.
Vin_6.285: One may carry a fan.
Vin_6.286: [He may use] a fan made of bark or a palm-leaf fan.
Vin_6.287: It must not be variegated or highly decorated.
Vin_6.288: The Saṃgha [may also use] other [fans].
Vin_6.289: One may give a jeweled fly-whisk that has arisen at a caitya.
Vin_6.290: This applies even to the disciple [of the Buddha].
Vin_6.291: One should maintain [images of] bull-figures, pillows, and square [carpets].
Vin_6.292. Upon obtaining a son or a wife, the conduct [regarding their status] is determined by the will of the giver. Vin_6.293.
If there is a ransom, its value shall be equal to the price [paid for them].
Vin_6.294. However, one may arrange for their eventual release.

Vin_6.295. If it is an ornament dedicated to a tree, its presentation as an adornment is for the sake of that very tree’s festival. Vin_6.296. If it is on a wall, it is for the purpose of painting. Vin_6.297. If not, it is for a pillar, for the purpose of new construction.
Vin_6.298: On the ground;
Vin_6.299: Making a fire-pit in a fire-hall; Vin_6.300: Or for the sake of obtaining oil.
Vin_6.301. Medicines are to be stored in the infirmary.
Vin_6.302. Food is to be prepared in the refectory. Vin_6.303. Drinks are to be kept in the water pavilion.
Vin_6.304: In a sauna hall, [the use] of a sauna or of an oily substance;
Vin_6.305: [The use] of an oily substance in a circular enclosure or in a storage hall;
Vin_6.306: Or digging with a shovel.
Vin_6.307: [The rule concerning] the vessel in the threshing-floor, the walkway, the gateway-chamber, and the pavilions; Vin_6.308: and also in the lotus-pond;
Vin_6.309: and the placing of this [vessel] as belonging to the Saṅgha of the four quarters—this is [the rule].
Vin_6.310. It is permissible to beg for the sake of precious materials. Vin_6.311. And there is a proclamation regarding the taking [of such materials].
Vin_6.312. A well-shelter with a door should be constructed for the purpose of seeing the wheel [of the Dharma], so that it is not afflicted by the calamities of heat, wind, and rain.
Vin_6.313 / [The rule] concerning one who possesses six [measures].
Vin_6.314 / The wearing of a large [robe] at the end of the festival.
Vin_6.315 / The concealment of profit by the guardian of the goods.
Vin_6.316: When two [items] are given for the worship of the Teacher, one must not enter among the nuns' community (*saṃghika*) without having designated them [for that purpose].
Vin_6.317: If they hear [the announcement] separately in a different assembly, there is a *sthūlātyaya* offense.
Vin_6.318: The vessel is [to be distributed] by the distributor of vessels (*bhāṇḍabhājaka*).
Vin_6.319: His consent is required.
Vin_6.320: Not for those who have not been purchased.
Vin_6.321: By means of an increase during the assembly of the Saṃgha.
In this case, the Elder of the Saṃgha must perform the valuation of that very [article] brought into the assembly;
[the same applies to] one of medium value.
Therefore, it does not follow that he is to be expelled.
Vin_6.325. Having determined it to be otherwise than it actually is, there is the downfall for one who increases [the value].
Vin_6.326. One who is not a buyer shall not increase [the price]. Vin_6.327. Nor [shall he increase it] regarding a woman.
Vin_6.328. One should not enjoy what belongs to another without its price having been paid. Vin_6.329. Nor should one prepare it [for oneself].
Vin_6.330. From the time the profit reaches ten [units] and above, it becomes the property of the heirs.
Vin_6.331. When something has been given to someone but not yet divided, if he dies, that portion goes to his fellow members.

Vin_6.332. One who has gone forth with the aspiration for Nirvāṇa and is virtuous deserves a garment worth a hundred thousand, food of a hundred flavors, a five-pillared gabled house, and the property of the Saṃgha. Vin_6.333. And the property of the Saṃgha.
Vin_6.334 / From one beyond training (aśaikṣa).
Vin_6.335 / Also from an ordinary person (pṛthagjana).
Vin_6.336 / Not from one of immoral conduct (duḥśīla).
Vin_6.337. For one who is indolent, living off the acceptance of gifts is like being in debt.
Vin_6.338. One who is worthy may live off the gains of an individual dwelling, provided that he does not depend on the gains of the Saṃgha within the boundary.
Vin_6.339. And this applies to one who is permanently assigned to a lodging.
Vin_6.340: Its distribution shall be by turn.

Vin_6.341: From among the iron vessels—namely, bowls, secondary bowls, ladles, water-pots, keys, knives, needles, nail-clippers, spoons, charcoal-stands, small pans, cooking pots, and frying pans—it must be distributed.
Vin_6.342: From among the earthenware vessels—namely, bowls, secondary bowls, cooking pots, small jars, water-pitchers, basins, water-vessels, and drinking cups—it must be distributed.
Vin_6.343: [The rule applies] to a bed made of precious materials or the like, but not to one made of iron; it applies to that which has been exchanged.
Vin_6.344: It does not apply to a wooden bed, nor to anything other than a fivefold dye.
Vin_6.345: Nor to that which has not been boiled.
Vin_6.346: The boiled [dye] is to be employed for coloring.
Vin_6.347: That which belongs to the Saṃgha.
Vin_6.348: The non-alteration of its arrival, its dwelling, and its objects—namely, the beds and seats.
Vin_6.349 / [The state of] being unfit to drink;
Vin_6.350 / and the state of not being subject to formal authorization;
Vin_6.351 / having partaken of the practice, one should maintain it by concealing it from one's parents.
Vin_6.352: If there is no gain of an extra bowl or robe, one should not cause [the donor] to give.
Vin_6.353: In the event that a meal-offering is not obtained, one should take half. This concludes the section on miscellaneous matters concerning robes. 2.
(Vin_6.3) [This concerns] what is included in the *Sapṛcchaka* and *Kṣudraka* sections. (Vin_6.354) For the purpose of knowing the distribution of robes,
(Vin_6.355) there is the giving of accumulations among these.
Vin_6.356. A small box with a lid for that purpose.
Vin_6.357. And for those who apply ointments.
Vin_6.358. From a fringe-tassel, the making of a bolster for those two.

Vin_6.359. There is no restriction regarding the cutting or the formal determination (*adhiṣṭhāna*) of the outer robe (*saṃghāṭī*), nor when those conditions for its form are absent, provided one desires it. Sitting and entering within a village or a house is permitted by this [rule].
Vin_6.360. The same applies to a dwelling of non-Buddhist ascetics (*tīrthya*).
Vin_6.361: One must not sit down while [the robes] are still present.
Vin_6.362: One should not resolve upon the three robes as being "hair-cloth. Vin_6.363: One should not use this for covering while eating.
Vin_6.364. Taking possession of a *viralikā* (a coarse woolen cloth).
Vin_6.365. It is of four kinds.
Vin_6.366. Namely: made of wool, made of linen, made of *dukūla* silk, and made of cotton.
Vin_6.367: And of other light cloths suitable for wearing, such as those made of *nikaṭara* wool and so forth;
Vin_6.368: and of *kocava* cloth;
Vin_6.369: one should not cause damage to the wool, otherwise one would be improperly using the garment.
Vin_6.370. One should not walk about while wearing this [robe] in such a manner.
Vin_6.371. An individual should not accept or make use of *aryāṇī*, *kocava*, *prāvāra*, or variegated *cilimilikā* rugs.
Vin_6.372. However, one may accept the laying down of a *cilimilikā* rug upon the walking path (*caṅkrama*).
Vin_6.373: One should not always walk while maintaining a single continuous stream [of attention].
Vin_6.374: If it is possible, one should perform repairs.
Vin_6.375: By means of providing [materials such as] hemp, bamboo, and bolts.
Vin_6.376. If it is impossible [to repair], one should apply cow-dung mud right there on the steps and plaster over them.
Vin_6.377. One may keep other items through the trust of a donor.
Vin_6.378. One should keep a lower garment (*nivāsana*), a side-covering cloth (*saṃkakṣikā*), and an upper side-covering cloth (*pratisaṃkakṣikā*).
Vin_6.379. And [this applies to] requisites and robes.
Vin_6.380. There is no fault in his being unskilled or in [the robe] having frayed borders.
Vin_6.381. This does not apply to what belongs to the Saṃgha.

Vin_6.382. Having performed the formal act of authorization (*adhiṣṭhāna*) and being permitted by the truth, one may wear the wearing of robes (*cīvaradhāraṇa*), even if it is only one from among the various types.
Vin_6.383. One should not perform the formal act of authorization for one whose mind is unstable.
Vin_6.384. Nor for one who has not received full ordination (*anupasaṃpanna*).
Vin_6.385 / Not directly perceived.
Vin_6.386 / There is no destruction of conceptual construction when one is situated in another place.
Vin_6.387 / Destruction [occurs] at the moment of death.
Vin_6.388 / [It is] among kinsmen.
Vin_6.389 / In this case, the owner is one who possesses the power of discretion.
Vin_6.390 / One should not take what has been relinquished as one's own.
Vin_6.391: One should relinquish it to a monk.
Vin_6.392: Not to the Saṃgha.
Vin_6.393: Not to one who is unlearned.
Vin_6.394: Begging for [a robe] when it is not given;
Vin_6.395: And taking [it] by force; Vin_6.396: Using a garment that has been perfumed with fragrances after having washed it.
Vin_6.397: Having beaten it with powders; Vin_6.398: having dried it out after treating it with oil; Vin_6.399:
one must not [use] the property belonging to the Saṃgha in the open air when it is raining.

Vin_6.400: One should not perform tasks such as washing, dyeing, making bowls, or splitting wood while in a state of intoxication. Vin_6.401: When the name of the recipient is not mentioned, a gift given to one who has cast it away after searching for it is not [valid]; nor is it [valid] when it is not cast away. One whose mind is not deranged may accept it from the house of a relative of that person or from the giver himself.
Vin_6.402: One may accept [a gift] from a son who has been sent away. Vin_6.403: And one may accept what has been brought back from a cemetery.
Vin_6.404: One seeks out a gift for him.

Vin_6.405. Furthermore, "taking" refers to the appropriation for one's own use of the property of a stūpa—excluding roots, fruits, and sugarcane—whether it be intended for food or as a source of livelihood, by setting it aside from its original purpose.
Vin_6.406. The inclusion of a gain occurs within the boundary of the rainy-season retreat (*varṣika-sīmā*).
Vin_6.407. One does not lose the status of being in retreat simply because the rains have been cut short.
Vin_6.408: Not when it has been thrown out.
Vin_6.409: Even for one who relies on a single part, that [is the case].
Vin_6.410: In this regard, the parts of the supports are according to their own enumeration.
Vin_6.411: In other cases where one has entered into multiple [orders], the determination is based on the majority.
Vin_6.412: In the case of obtaining gains, the novice monk and the novice nun receive a third less than the others. Vin_6.413: Regarding edible food, they receive an equal share.
Vin_6.414. And [the same applies] to those seeking full ordination and to *śikṣamāṇās*.
Vin_6.415. The distribution of shares for the *bhikṣuṇīs* is according to individuals (*pudgalaśas*), not as a collective (*saṃghaśas*).
Vin_6.416. There is no eating of food that has not been formally set aside; if the *bhikṣuṇīs* have already eaten, one must not enter there to obtain further gains.

Vin_6.417. Regarding seats, water, and alms-food, there is no seniority for a monk among the nuns. Vin_6.418. There is release from the rule concerning the seat when nuns sit together with monks at the end of the row of elders.
Vin_6.419. When it is impossible [to provide] the service of being among the monks, the nun shall assign the gift; she shall distribute the food equally, [standing] with feet placed [on the ground].
The elder of the Saṅgha should appoint [someone] for the purpose of giving.
Having observed the assembly according to its capacity—whether the food is abundant or scant—he should first announce that;
otherwise, he should act according to his own means. Vinaya 6.420–421.
Vin_6.422. And when the announcement has not been made, one should not take [the portion] at the head of the elders, thinking, "I have arrived.
Vin_6.423. When food has been prepared and others have arrived after those for whom it was intended, that [arrival] must be reported.
Vin_6.424. One should not urge a monk toward the giving of the three robes.
Vin_6.425. This does not apply while [the person] is still alive.
Vin_6.426. Since it is said "it shall be returned," the Saṃgha should accept it with a different intention. Vin_6.427.
With the inner and outer robes, there is the discarding of what belongs to the deceased.
Vin_6.428: With the middle [part]. Vin_6.429: Not with what remains.
This concludes the section on robes concerning those that require inquiry and minor items, etc. (3).
And the section on robes is completed. 6.
*Vin_7, Chapter on Leather:
Vin_7.1 / The boundaries of the Middle Country;
Vin_7.2 / To the east is the forest grove named Puṇḍakakṣa, in front of Puṇḍravardhana.
To the south of Śarāvatī is the river named Tadupākhyā; to the west are the two Brāhmaṇa villages, Sthūṇa and Upasthūṇa;
and to the north is Mount Uśīra.
Vin_7.6 One should wear sandals in a border region. Vin_7.7 And for the purpose of protecting the bedding and seating.
Vin_7.8 [These sandals] should have a single layer of leather.
Vin_7.9 / Repairing by means of providing a hinge.
Vin_7.10 / Not [repairing] the interior of the folds.
Vin_7.11 / Even if it has many folds, it is [considered repaired] once it has been used by a householder for as few as seven steps.
Vin_7.12: When the purpose is merely to make what is unallowable allowable, the taking of it is not considered "final" by virtue of its connection to that purpose.
Vin_7.13: It is not [considered final] if it is variegated or embroidered.
Vin_7.14: Nor is it [considered final] if it has the appearance of a horn.
Vin_7.15 / Not one made of *aśvattha* or *karavīra* leaves.
Vin_7.16 / Not one inlaid with gold or silver.
Vin_7.17 / Not one that makes a *kicikica* sound.
Vin_7.18 / Not making a *kiṇikiṇa* sound; Vin_7.19 / not making a *khiṇikhiṇa* sound;
Vin_7.20 / not making a *jhiṇijhiṇa* sound.
Vin_7.21 / Or [it applies to] one who displays other forms of arrogance.
Vin_7.22 / There is no unallowability for the act of killing animals. Vin_7.23 / One should hold [the robe] in front, with the palms joined at the back.

Vin_7.25 / And [he should not wear] a shaven head or a *pūlā* (hair-tuft). Vin_7.26 / And in a country where people live in huts, he may wear a *kholā* (head-covering) or a *pūlā*. Vin_7.27 / He should not engage in the use of footwear in the presence of one who is venerable.

Vin_7.28. One must not have anything placed upon the body of a lion, a tiger, a leopard, an elephant, or a noble steed (*ājāneya*). Vin_7.29. This includes the armpit, the trunk [of an elephant], and the hump; by these terms, other fierce wild animals are also implied.
Vin_7.30. One must not clap one's hands.
Vin_7.31. One should wipe it with a coarse cloth for the sake of removing dust.
Vin_7.32. One should keep it. Vin_7.33. One should sew it together.
Vin_7.34. One should construct a sheltered place for items not intended for display.
Vin_7.35. For that purpose, one should keep a cord and a binding strap.
Vin_7.36. Not a needle-case.
Vin_7.37. One should not mount a wooden sandal, except within a house or in a privy.
Vin_7.38. Nor [should one mount sandals made of] bamboo leaves, muñja grass, śirī grass, or darbha grass. Vin_7.39. Nor [should one mount a sandal] made of rope.
Vin_7.40. When there is no wind or blood [to cause irritation].
Vin_7.41. One should sit upon a hide; in its absence, one should place it inside the house.
Vin_7.42. Even in this case, even when such conditions exist, there is no offense. One should accept a tiger skin for the sake of the eyes.
Vin_7.43 / Placing it at the place of the feet.
Vin_7.44 / At the door of the Perfume Chamber for the Buddha.
Vin_7.45 / Covering the sandals.
Vin_7.46. Sitting and reclining in the wind—this entire procedure is for the application [of treatment] in cases of hemorrhoids.
Vin_7.47. One should know that [the benefit] arises from the contact with the hair. Vin_7.48. And by means of having many folds, [it serves as] a poultice.
Vin_7.49: And even by one person standing over many [monks].
Vin_7.50: One should not wear leather in the regions beyond the border (Anasmāparāntaka).
Vin_7.51: Nor that of a lion or similar animals.
Vin_7.52. Even the sinews, bones, teeth, flesh, and shoulder-blades of that [animal] whose hide is unallowable are likewise unallowable.
Vin_7.53. One should wear [the garment] three times [dyed].
Vin_7.54. It should be saffron-colored or like that of a young brahmin.
Vin_7.55 / Not variegated or multi-colored.
Vin_7.56 / One should not, having placed a rug over it, dive into deep water.
Vin_7.57 / One should train in swimming in a secluded place.
Vin_7.58. One should not lean against a hero in deep water, except for a bull.
Vin_7.59. One may lean against an elephant, a horse, a buffalo, or a king.
[Thus ends] the section on leather, [numbered] 7.
*Vinaya-vastu 8: The Chapter on Medicines* / (Vinaya-vastu 8.1) One may consume medicine.

Vin_8.2: This [offense] is of four kinds. Vin_8.3: It concerns one who is not ill and it is not the first time. Vin_8.4: And it concerns all [liquids] such as *ucchu* (sugarcane juice), *mocaka*, *kola*, *aśvattha*, *udumbara*, *puruṣaka*, *mṛdvīkā*, *kharjūra*, and drinks.

Vin_8.5 Likewise, fermented gruel, whey from curdled milk, and the scum of boiled rice—these, when separated from water, strained through cloth, clear, transparent enough to see one's face, and the color of a reed stalk;
Vin_8.6 it is improper for one who has previously been ordained to [partake of these] with one who has subsequently received ordination and possesses the same gender.
Vin_8.7 [This applies to] the five items beginning with *harītakī*.
Vin_8.8 / And [the same applies] to molasses.
Vin_8.9 / Regarding the consumption of this when it has been formally authorized, the status of being "sick" applies to the overseer of stores, the storekeeper, and those performing new construction.
Vin_8.10 / This also applies to one whose meal has been interrupted, and to the non-timely consumption of food.
Vin_8.11 / [It concerns] drinks that are not yet fermented.
Vin_8.12 / [Drinks that are] clear.
Vin_8.13 / Because that substance is not yet [fermented], if it is temporary, there is no offense for one who has not received full ordination to crush it and strain it through a cloth.
Vin_8.14: Regarding these substances, [the rule applies] to others besides the pomegranate and the citron.
Vin_8.15: If it is of the *kālika* (temporary) type, its limit is the end of the watch (*yāmānta*).
Vin_8.16: If it is of another type, [the limit is] that which pertains to it.

Vin_8.17: One [view] holds that this [rule] applies when there is no transgression, because it is a transgression when one does cross [the limit]. Vin_8.18: That is incorrect, because it would depend on a time beyond [the limit], and since that state would have been attained, it would be unapproachable; furthermore, it would result in the future ordinary [monks] being unable to take formal possession [of the robes].
Vin_8.19: In this context, "having entered" refers to the juice, the powder, and the *ariṣṭa* (fermented liquor).
Vin_8.20: And of clear sauvīraka (sour gruel).
Vin_8.21: Medicines such as *pūla* and so forth are those boiled and cooked.
Vin_8.22: Ghee, oil, honey, and molasses may be kept for seven days.
Vin_8.23: All [substances] such as molasses, sugar-candy, and granulated sugar are included under the category of *phāṇita* (unrefined treacle). Vin_8.24: [The same applies to] ghee and earth.
Vin_8.25: [The same applies to] the oils of the five types of domesticated animals.
Vin_8.26 / [The consumption of] fish, meat, and cold [drinks] is permitted for those who are guarding or for those who are pigs.
Vin_8.27 / When not ill, there is no use for them;
Vin_8.28 / when healthy, one commits an offense by giving them away under the pretext of illness.
Vin_8.29. In the absence of these, [one may use] a decoction from a sick-room and medicinal ointments.
Vin_8.30. Root, stem, leaf, and fruit are for life-long use for the purpose of medicine, provided they are not intoxicants;
for example: nut-grass (*musta*), sweet flag (*vacā*), turmeric, fresh ginger, and ativiṣā. Vin_8.31. That is to say: nut-grass, sweet flag, turmeric, fresh ginger, and ativiṣā.
Sandalwood, *cavikā*, *padmaka*, *guḍūcī*, *devadāru*, turmeric, and fresh ginger;
the leaves of *vāsaka*, *keśātakī*, *paṭola*, *nimba*, and *saptaparṇa*; and the flowers of *vāsaka*, *nimba*, *dhātakī*, and *nāga*, as well as the filaments of the lotus.
Haritakī, āmalaka, bibhītaka, marīca, and pippalī; lac;
for example, asafoetida and sarjarasa.
Vin_8.38: *stapaḥ*, *stapakarṇī*, *stapakaraḥ*.
Vin_8.39: *kṣāraḥ*.
Vin_8.40: For example, those of sesame leaves, soda ash, barley-alkali, and *vāsaka*.
Vin_8.41: And alkaline substances. Vin_8.42: Salt. Vin_8.43:
Such as rock salt, black salt, biḍa salt, sea salt, and Romaka salt.
Vin_8.44: Astringent decoctions (kaṣāya).
Vin_8.45: Such as those of the mango, the neem, the koṣāmba, the śirīṣa, and the jambu trees.

Vin_8.47: There is no limit to the taking of medicine for one who has undergone a change in their diet.

Vin_8.50: [A bowl] made of clay; Vin_8.51: or that which is made from gold, yellow *śāla* wood, *aśvattha*, *udumbara*, or *nyagrodha* wood;

Vin_8.53 / Taking from a lay follower who has faith.

Vin_8.56. From this, there is the taking up of all things. Vin_8.57. This constitutes its purpose.

Vin_8.58. If, when the time for using it has passed, they should distribute the medicine prepared by the solicitor for the sake of one who is aged, emaciated, or suffering from dysentery, he shall not consume it for any other purpose.

Vin_8.62: Its existence also pertains to others, because of the current practice; therefore, one should proceed to assist it according to the previous method. Vin_8.64: It is accomplished through washing, just as when rice grains are processed, the state of remaining [pure] is counted as its own measure, like molasses.
Vin_8.65: Regarding molasses, the practice is as with molasses.

Vin_8.67: Until the end of the horse-feeding period.
Vin_8.68: [Food] received before the morning meal.

Vin_8.71. There is no established practice of formal authorization (*adhiṣṭhāna*) regarding food that has not been formally accepted, food kept overnight, food not formally received by another, or food cooked by a monk after it was already cooked.

Vin_8.74: The illustration is the sequence of medicines.

Vin_8.76: Not for the purpose of non-medicine.

Vin_8.78: [A small box] for *goṇikā-guḍikā-añjana*.
Vin_8.79: [A small box] for *goṇikā-guḍikā-añjana*.
Vin_8.80: A tube for flower-paste, powders, and collyriums.
Vin_8.81: One should carry a probe.
Vin_8.82: It should be made of copper or iron, or of precious gems.

Vin_8.83. One who is afflicted by illness may carry a leather bag for the purpose of storing medicine. Vin_8.84. In that case, one's own [leather] may be used, or a sack or a container may be made heavy with it.
Vin_8.85. By means of drying it from time to time, there shall be no putrefaction of what has been stored.
Vin_8.86: In shade and sun.
Vin_8.87: There is loss when the vigor is dried up.

Vin_8.89: One should carry a medicine-cup.
Vin_8.90: A medicine-bag. Vin_8.91: And a drinking-scarf for when one is fainting.
Vin_8.92: [It is permitted] for one who is ill [to use] salt.
Vin_8.93: For one with a fistula, it is proper to have a place prepared with a vessel.
Vin_8.94: [It is permitted] for one who has been boiled with cow dung.
Vin_8.95: The giving [of earth] to Vidhānaka so that there may be no fault arising from its absence.
Vin_8.96: Only for one who is not absorbed in it.
Vin_8.97: Earth for those who have used scents.
One may consume even a ball of food. All [of this] should be used.
Regarding the chain, it is for the purpose of lifting up that which is heated; there, it is attached.
Vin_8.101: When heating [the bowl], one should support it with moist clay.
Vin_8.102: There is no staying [of the bowl] while there is an application of food-remnants.
Vin_8.103: First the heating of the permissible [bowl], and afterwards that of the one for use.
Vin_8.104: A vessel for one who has been treated with enemas.
Vin_8.105: In this case, it is a grave offense if, due to impossibility otherwise, there is a failure to restore [the patient].
Vin_8.106: In this matter, a tube made of gemstone or metal is appropriate; that of iron is not.
Vin_8.107. Likewise, [it is forbidden] to perform medical treatment with a surgical instrument.
Vin_8.108. One should not apply anything other than this [medicine] to the mouth for a long period.
Vin_8.109. Nor should one perform the excision of hemorrhoids.
Vin_8.110: Even by means other than a weapon; Vin_8.111: [nor] by means of spells or medicinal herbs, should one cause them to be examined; Vin_8.112: one who is corrupted should not treat [them].
Vin_8.113: It is improper to consume food at night when there is doubt [regarding its suitability].

Vin_8.114: In this case, it should not be suspected that what has not been formally offered or what has been stored is unfit for consumption. Vin_8.115: For the purpose of dispelling doubt, drinking [medicinal substances] is permitted; this is accomplished by means of incense sticks and a funnel.

Vin_8.116: Making it out of iron. Vin_8.117: It is proper that it be twelve finger-breadths [in length], not sharp, nor [used] by men. Vin_8.118: Placing it in a bag after having smeared it with ghee or oil.
Vin_8.119: Its placement is on a peg for hanging clothes or on a bamboo rack for robes. Vin_8.120: It may be thrown into the fire for the purpose of cleansing it.
Vin_8.121: The administration of nasal therapy is permitted.
Vin_8.122: There is no failure [of the rule] regarding the loss of the instrument. Vin_8.123: It is good if it has two sharp points. Vin_8.124:
This is the reason for it.
Vin_8.125: One may consume meat that is not [normally] eaten for the sake of medicine.
Vin_8.126: For one who has become attached to eating it, there is a means [of restraint]. Vin_8.127: Covering the eyes with a cloth.
Vin_8.128: Anointing with a fragrant substance [is permitted] so that it does not arise [as an offense].
Vin_8.129: When the state of being obsessed has departed and one remains established in it, there is the release of pleasant food and drink in the presence [of the recipient].
Vin_8.130: It is a gross [offense] if, for another purpose, one puts it into his mouth.

Vin_8.131: In all cases, [it is forbidden] regarding human flesh. Vin_8.132: Knowing that meat has been prepared specifically for oneself, one should not eat it. Vin_8.133: Nor [should one eat] the remains of a tiger's meal.
Vin_8.134: Not [the flesh] of elephants, horses, or serpents.

Vin_8.135: Nor that of one-hoofed animals, jackals, monkeys, crows, *kaṭaka* birds, vultures, cranes, *bhaṣaka* dogs, owls, or any other carnivorous birds; nor that of insects, spiders, or worms found in excrement, vomit, or filth.
Vin_8.136: Meat that has been rejected becomes [forbidden]; one who causes it to be accepted should be questioned.
Vin_8.137: The first [offense occurs] when there is multiplicity.
Vin_8.138: [The offense occurs] when causing it to be inserted within.
Vin_8.139. Even the drinking of elephant milk and human milk is permitted.
Vin_8.140. However, it is not an offense for one who is ill to use eye-salve, collyrium, or ointments applied to the eyes, provided they are not substances forbidden as food.
Vin_8.141. For one who is fainting due to illness, even such things may be drunk.
[The use of] honey and oil [is permitted] for one who does not drink intoxicants. There is no fault in this when it is not an intoxicant.
Its preparation is from a decoction.

Vin_8.145. When roasted barley that has been thrown [into a vat] is placed on the ground, it becomes edible if it has become sour; it remains inedible otherwise. Vin_8.146. It becomes inedible. Vin_8.147. Grape juice becomes intoxicating through boiling.
Vin_8.148 / There is no existence [of a thing] when it is not separated [from its cause].
Vin_8.149 / Existence is the state of being a latent impression (*vāsanā*).

Vin_8.150 / "Drink" refers to medicinal roots, tubers, leaves, flowers, and fruits that have been permeated by the scent of intoxicants, as well as dried powders and water, for the purpose of removing the craving for intoxicants.
Vin_8.151: When the vessel is full, one should dilute it by adding water.
Vin_8.152: Contact with [the intoxicant] must be avoided; therefore, when it is deficient [in strength], and when its potency has departed, Vin_8.153:
likewise by making it tasteless, and by drinking it at an improper time, or with food.
Vin_8.154. It is good that it be pleasing; therefore, it should be made beautiful with white thread.
Vin_8.155. Even if one is ill, one must not drink intoxicants, even as much as a drop on the tip of a blade of kusha grass.
Vin_8.156. And there must be no giving of anything whatsoever by a lay follower.
Vin_8.157: Except for the purpose of medical treatment—this remainder applies to all cases involving natural offenses (*prakṛtisāvadya*).
Vin_8.158: One shall not consume garlic, onion, or leek.
Vin_8.159: A sick person [may do so] in a secluded place.

Vin_8.160. One who is not using [medicine] should not consume garlic for seven days, onions for three nights, or *gṛñjana* for one night; nor should he consume [garlic] in a monastery. Vin_8.161. [This applies to] bedding and seating. Vin_8.162. He must not enter a latrine.
Vin_8.163: Not in a urinal.
Vin_8.164: One should not enter into the midst of the Saṃgha. Vin_8.165: Nor in the precincts of a shrine.
Vin_8.166: You should take pleasure in moderation.
Vin_8.167: One should not teach the Dharma to householders. Vin_8.168: One should not frequent families to the point of causing their ruin.
Vin_8.169: Not in places crowded with people. Vin_8.170: Bathing at the end [of the rainy season]. Vin_8.171: And the removal of the odor from the robes.
Vin_8.172: By means of fumigation and incense.
Vin_8.173: Life-prolonging [medicines] during a famine. Vin_8.174: That which is consecrated as permissible for an ox, a crow, or a bird.

Vin_8.175. One should not take formal possession (*adhiṣṭhā*) of the site of a tree-root, an elephant-stable, a heretical dwelling, or a royal palace; nor of a nunnery, a rainy-season retreat, a threshing floor, a gatehouse, a storeroom, a palace, a sauna, a maintenance hall, an open-air space, a fire-hall, a shrine-site, or the property of a householder that is beyond the shrine.
Vin_8.176. [The same applies to] the property of a householder that is beyond the shrine.
Vin_8.177: Even the cooking of food is not a cause for [a formal act] here.
Vin_8.178: And there are five types of utensils.
Vin_8.179: There are four periods of time during the night.
Vin_8.180: For him, the first eight days constitute the period of *mānāpya*; thereafter, it is the state of being subject to the *navakarma*. Vin_8.181:
Otherwise, it is the state of not having obtained the consent (*adhivāsana*) of the monks.
Vin_8.182: There is the attainment of the monks' consent for his removal from that [period].
Vin_8.183: Its reality [is established] by way of its form, its commencement, and its cessation.
Vin_8.184: Everywhere, the Saṃgha [is defined] by means of formal action (karman).
Vin_8.185: In the first two cases, the individual (pudgala) is also [included].
Vin_8.186 / One who performs new construction work;
Vin_8.187 / He alone [is the one] at the beginning;
Vin_8.188 / By means of speaking.
Vin_8.189: In the second instance of formal determination, it concerns a great number of monks.
Vin_8.190: As many as are present, in the fourth instance, [it concerns] the Saṃmaṃkalpika hall through the utterance of speech expressing intention.

Vin_8.191: It is not improper for others to perform work for the sake of a single person’s vehicle or dwelling. Vin_8.192: This is not said to be permissible for one who has become separated [from the community]. Vin_8.193: A monk may eat food that has been cooked and taken up after it was received.
Vin_8.194 / [Eating] before the meal; Vin_8.195 / [Drinking] gruel at all times;
Vin_8.196 / [Eating] what was not previously offered, having risen from one's seat.
Vin_8.197: One should rise at that time for the sake of the last [meal].
Vin_8.198: The remainder.
Vin_8.199: That which has been brought forth.
Vin_8.200: One should remove it.
Vin_8.201: [The rule concerning] forest-dwelling monks.
Vin_8.202: That which is designated by that name.
Vin_8.203: For example: grapes, pomegranates, dates, figs, *vātāma*, *urumāna*, *rāmāpikā*, *kurumāyikā*, *nikoca*, *babhūḥ*, *piñcitikā*, and that which is called *puṣkara*.
Vin_8.204: For example: *vinmaṃ*, lotus stalks, *veṭṭa*, lotus roots (*śālūka*), and lotus seeds (*padmakarkaṭikā*).
[Thus ends] the Bhaiṣajyavastu, section one.
**(Vin_8.2) Regarding the section on minor matters:
Vin_8.205. One should not accept half of a kingdom.
Vin_8.206. One may accept villages for the sake of the Saṃgha.**
Vin_8.207 / And the field [is also to be given].
Vin_8.208 / They should not neglect this.
Vin_8.209 / Its gift is by means of enjoyment.
Vin_8.210: The seeking of fortune. Vin_8.211: Because of his blackness, he is not to be led into the monastery. Vin_8.212: First [he should be led] from his own [place].
Vin_8.213: An appointment of monks shall be made for the sake of protection.

Vin_8.214: If the expenditure is not clearly understood due to fear or one of the other [causes], one should seek an accounting elsewhere than from memory. Vin_8.215: Otherwise, it is through mindfulness.
One should proceed there preceded by Prajñapti;
one should accept attendants for the sake of the Saṃgha.
Since sound does not reach there, the construction of a monastery is permitted.

Vin_8.218. If food is to be given, it should be prepared for the sake of the ritual act. Vin_8.219. Cows, buffaloes, goats, sheep, elephants, horses, camels, donkeys, grain, and vessels—these are not to be assigned to a stūpa; they are not to be considered as belonging to it. Vin_8.220.
One may keep [for oneself] small pieces of cloth, salt, and reddish-brown garments.
Vin_8.221. A person should not possess any bronze vessel other than a waist-belt and a drinking-cup.
Vin_8.222. He should have a monastery attendant provide it.
Vin_8.223. Taking hold of it is for the sake of protection, even when handing it over to others of the same gender.
Vin_8.224. Their dress consists of having a robe hanging around their necks.
Vin_8.225. Or, out of a compassionate disposition, they carry it on their hips. Vin_8.226. That is the taking up of what has been brought by a relative.
Vin_8.227 / And at the end, because of its being a means of escape;
Vin_8.228 / and because of their gratitude;
Vin_8.229 / one should not ask for this price.
Vin_8.230. One may take possession of the acquisition of fruit.
Vin_8.231. [One may take possession of] jars of ghee, oil, honey, and molasses.
Vin_8.232. And also their containers.

Vin_8.233. One should place it on a stand. Vin_8.234. It is not to be used for [ordinary] consumption; it is for excrement and urine, and for jars. Vin_8.235. One should attend to the needs of the Saṃgha regarding the preparation and cooking of food.
Vin_8.236. One should not go out for alms with the bowl placed at one’s side before the meal has begun.
Vin_8.237. One should hold the bowl while consuming the alms-food.
Vin_8.238. There is no doubt that, in this case, there is a lack of commonality regarding the holding of metal vessels.
Vin_8.239: And it is improper for a sick woman to possess clothing or ornaments.
Vin_8.240: One should not enter a family for alms with a vessel that makes a noise.
Vin_8.241: One should carry this [vessel].
Vin_8.242: One should strive for skill in exiting and entering [houses].
Vin_8.243: One should not engage in alms-gathering by means of making signs with the hands or other such gestures.
Vin_8.244: One should not make a living through the trade of the Dharma.
Vin_8.245. If water is unavailable, one should wash the feet with the scum of curd and so forth.
Vin_8.246. One should sit upon a grass mat.
Vin_8.247. One should place it in a secluded, open space.
Vin_8.248: Even by piling them into a heap.
Vin_8.249: At the end, there is measuring.
Vin_8.250: The making [of it] is for the sake of abundance, due to the multiplicity of the planks.
Vin_8.251: [The offense is incurred] by groups of five hundred.
Vin_8.252: The subsequent provision is made until the end of the increase.
Vin_8.253: Or, when those who authorized [the construction] act as thieves, it constitutes an *uddeśa* (formal assignment).
Vin_8.254: First, the distribution of food is to be handled by those appointed for the service of meals.

Vin_8.257. One should go to the head of the meal with little noise.
Vin_8.258. [One should eat] with well-restrained [senses]. Vin_8.259. [One should be] pleasing to look at.
Vin_8.260. One should stand in this manner.
Vin_8.261. One should not step with the foot upon anything that is to be consumed. Vin_8.262. Nor should one do so when it touches the base of the bowl.

Vin_8.263. Having established mindfulness, one should receive alms-food with an undistracted mind. Vin_8.264. One should not scatter [food] into the bowl beyond what is required. Vin_8.265. One should not mix [the food] together.
Vin_8.266 / Not in haste;
Vin_8.267 / well-concealed;
Vin_8.268 / one should carry it out at a time that is not too late.
Vin_8.269: There is no impropriety in accepting what is obtained from someone other than the one with whom one has made a formal agreement.

Vin_8.270: There is no fault in eating food that was intended for oneself but has been offered by another. Vin_8.271: Just as if it were included within that [original gift], it is permitted for one who is seated at an invitation from another to eat what is given by that other person.

Vin_8.272. When employing words for a desired purpose, it is established by what is well-known. Vin_8.273. One should not abandon the "end" (*anta*). With respect to those endowed with right view and virtue, the "end" is respectively the giving of what is surplus and the taking of food sufficient for sustenance from one who does not eat leftovers. Vin_8.274. And there is the ruin of enjoyments consisting of what has been given in faith.

Vin_8.275: For one who has touched alms-food out of consideration for his mother, father, a sick person, a child, or a pregnant woman, as well as for a layperson who has arrived, he should share it with them. Vin_8.276:
He should set aside mouthfuls of food.
Vin_8.277: He should eat without interruption.
Vin_8.278. And one should not give to a person of the animal realm.
Vin_8.279. One should not give from what has been set aside for the sake of devotion to one who lacks self-control.
Vin_8.280. When there is an invitation, it is not a violation of the trust placed in the bowl if one eats the leavings as a means of making oneself comfortable.
Vin_8.281: An offering of food is to be made to the resident monks.
Vin_8.282: This is done according to their respective traditions during the morning session and so forth. Vin_8.283: If they belong to different traditions, it is to be done separately.
Vin_8.284. One should not eat a mango that has reached the state of being worm-eaten or shriveled.

Vin_8.285. There is no [rule regarding] the unfitness of roots, stalks, leaves, flowers, fruits, edible greens, boiled rice, sour gruel, parched grain, meat, cakes, milk, curd, butter, fish, and dried meat.
Vin_8.286: There is no prohibition against rice gruel made from roots, tubers, leaves, flowers, fruits, and so forth, provided that the ingredients are not suspected of being poisonous.
Vin_8.287: Even water may serve as a strengthening tonic for a messenger.
Vin_8.288: There is no unfitness [for consumption] in that which has reached the state of satiation.
Vin_8.289: It is permissible to eat food from a vessel.
Vin_8.290: [It is permissible] from a silver one.
Vin_8.291: And from one made of stone.
Vin_8.292: Even when one has finished eating, the activity of attending to [the bowl] is not a violation regarding cleansing.
Vin_8.293: This also applies even after one has eaten.
Vin_8.294: One should not eat from a single vessel together with another person.
Vin_8.295. When it is impossible for the monks to eat from their own vessels while on a journey, [the food] should be placed in the hands of another.
Vin_8.296. Once it has been lifted, one should place one's own portion into the hand of another.
Vin_8.297. When sharing with a *śrāmaṇera*, if there is a connection with others, the donors should give by combining [their portions] into a single mass.
Vin_8.298: When requested by a kinsman out of affection in every respect; Vin_8.299: in a secluded place;
Vin_8.300: [the offense applies] regarding protection against improper acceptance, what has been stolen, what has been caused to be accepted improperly, and what is mixed with such things.
Vin_8.301. One should not eat while wearing sandals.
Vin_8.302. [The rule applies] even when one is ill, provided one has stepped upon them. Vin_8.303. One should not eat naked or with only a single robe.

Vin_8.304. There is no offense if the attendant of one who is ill provides for his protection. Vin_8.305. If he is able, he should resort to a *saṃkakṣikā* (breast-cloth). Vin_8.306. And [he should resort to] a secluded place.
Vin_8.307. One should not, for the sake of food, signal to a server who is seated nearby by saying, "Give this to me" or "Give that.
Vin_8.308. There is no offense in the case of one who is ill, provided it was not said [for the purpose of obtaining food].
Vin_8.309. For example, as when one with weak digestion perceives raw food cooked over a mild fire as being fit for one who is ill, or as when one with a strong digestive fire perceives it as such.
Vin_8.310: One should eat after having established mindfulness, maintaining the perception of food as medicine. Vin_8.311: And one should maintain mindfulness. Vin_8.312:

[One should reflect on] its similarity to the process of digestion, its nature as an adversary, its being a natural outflow, its dependence on conditions, its dependence on ritual preparation and seeking, its dependence on others, its lack of harmlessness, its individuality, and its extreme state of repulsiveness.
Vin_8.313 / With mindfulness established; Vin_8.314 / Undistracted; Vin_8.315 / Fully aware and making little noise.
Vin_8.316 / Not doing this;
Vin_8.317 / Not causing [the recipient] to consume the gruel;
Vin_8.318 / Without making a smacking sound.
Vin_8.319: Softening [the sound] of those things that produce noise, such as water and so forth, [is permissible].
Vin_8.320: It is not [permissible] when it is being played for the purpose of eating. Vin_8.321:
Nor [is it permissible] when it is being played for the sake of instruction by one who has experienced [the teaching].
Vin_8.322: After the time has passed, [one may speak] for the sake of the two applications of the meaning.
Vin_8.323: Having eaten, one should recite a verse.
Vin_8.324: After eating an invitation, there is the performance of the dedication of merit and the teaching of the Dharma.
Vin_8.325 / Having ascertained that all [monks] have finished eating;
Vin_8.326 / by means of looking around;
Vin_8.327 / in the case of plurality, by the first [method].
Vin_8.328. If [the recipient] is unable, one should request a capable person [to go].
Vin_8.329. If the reason for going has not been fulfilled, there shall be the giving of an escort to the monks.
Vin_8.330. At least four [monks] must be provided.
Vin_8.331. When there is a reason for going, one should look at one's teeth.
Vin_8.332. In the instruction regarding the offering to Nanda and Upananda, their names are to be mentioned.
Vin_8.333. Regarding things to be swallowed: having first spat out two or three strands of saliva, phlegm, or mucus, and having wiped the mouth clean.
Vin_8.334. This is not non-food.
Vin_8.335. Therefore, one who has been invited at an improper time and delights in belching should have another person wash his mouth.
Vin_8.336. One should not discharge phlegm in a place where it has not been designated for that purpose.
Vin_8.337: Not while it is being prepared. Vin_8.338: One should not present this *chanda* (consent) in the presence of an elder. Vin_8.339: Nor while he is eating.
Vin_8.340: Nor [is it an offense] for one who has been instructed again and again.
Vin_8.341: If one is unable [to act] due to another, there is no fault in departing.
Vin_8.342: There is no fault in not making contact with another.
Vin_8.344. While walking, one should not proceed by another [path].
Vin_8.345. The bowl of one who shares [it] has a base shaped like an elephant's foot. Vin_8.346. One should place it in this manner.
Vin_8.347. One should maintain screens made of water, sand, or shade to ward off flies.
Vin_8.348. It should be washed and dried from time to time so that it does not become foul-smelling and so that living beings do not breed within it.
Vin_8.349. For that purpose, another [screen] should be provided when needed.
