Vin_17.206. There is also a lattice-work on the wall of the monastery belonging to the renunciants, and the walls have circular openings for the discharge of water.
Vin_17.208: And [this applies] to the enclosure and the moat.
Vin_17.209: And the dwelling of an individual (pudgala), together with its appurtenances.

Vin_17.210: The preparation consists of making the walls of the dwellings manifest as the signs of the "totality" (kṛtsna) meditations on blue and so forth, according to the fourfold classification of blue and the rest.
(17.211) Decorating the monastery.
(17.212) It is permissible for the monastery of those who have gone forth to be decorated;
at the gate, there may be paintings of yakṣas with hands holding the vajra and other implements.
Vin_17.213: [The depiction] of the wheel of saṃsāra in the gateway chamber.
Vin_17.214: The making of the fivefold [depiction of] the tumor.
Vin_17.215: [The depiction] of gods and humans above.
[The Buddha spoke] regarding the four continents.
Regarding spontaneously born beings, as they pass away and are reborn like a waterwheel, [the Teacher] showed the forms of a pigeon, a snake, and a pig for passion, hatred, and delusion;
[he showed] the former two being devoured by delusion.
Vin_17.219: [He should teach] the twelvefold dependent origination in its preliminary context.
Vin_17.220: [He should show that] everything is seized by impermanence.
Vin_17.221: Above that, he should point out the pure circle of Nirvana belonging to the Buddha.
Vin_17.222: "The two verses have begun" refers to the portion below those two [verses].
Vin_17.223: This is the placement of the narrator.
Vin_17.224: It concerns the vicinity of the Great Miracle and the breaking of Māra.
Vin_17.225: [The seat] for those born in the palace;
Vin_17.226: for the Mālādhāra Yakṣas at the door of the Gandhakuṭī; Vin_17.227: in the assembly hall, [the seat] for the row of elders.
Vin_17.228: At the gate of the monastery compound, [he saw] yakṣas with sprouts in their hands. Vin_17.229: In the dining hall, [he saw] those with food in their hands.
Vin_17.230: In the steam-heated bathhouse, [he saw] kumbhāṇḍas with sprouts and grass in their hands, who were tending the fire-islands.
Vin_17.231: In the fire-hall, there were the Kumbhāṇḍaputras, who applied dark pigments and the like and kindled the fire.
Vin_17.232: There was Devadūtī, holding the lamp for the donor (dānapati), and she for whom [the lamp was intended].
Vin_17.233: And in the water-pavilion, there were Naga maidens adorned with various ornaments, holding jars in their hands, pouring out water.

Vin_17.234. [The Buddha] was attending to the Tathāgata’s illness in the infirmary. Vin_17.235. [He was also attending to him] at the latrine, the urinal, the cemetery, or by a human skull. Vin_17.236. One should not make or maintain a fire with smoke inside a monastery or in an open space; everything may be done on a paved floor or a terrace.
Vin_17.237. One should keep a small brush for that purpose.
Vin_17.238. And one should keep an iron rod with a flat head for the purpose of smoothing [the hair].
Vin_17.239. This purpose may also be accomplished by means of a wooden *ḍhiṃsuka*.
Vin_17.240. The officer in charge of the monastery grounds should sweep the vihāra every day. Vin_17.241.
If he is unable to do so daily, he should sweep the areas currently being used.
Vin_17.242. On the remaining days—the eighth and the fourteenth—he should strike the ghaṇṭā for the entire Saṅgha, and then attend by means of a Dharma discourse, noble silence, or remaining quiet.
Vin_17.243: At a Dharma festival, there is anointing, and the offering of soft cow-dung balls for one who is delicate.
Vin_17.244: Bathing with *antare*. Vin_17.245: Or washing the hands and feet.
Vin_17.246: Rubbing the body with water-smeared [hands]. Vin_17.247: Causing the acquisition of oiliness.
Vin_17.248: Jumping over objects that have been polished or cleansed for the sake of jewels—such as incense mounds, images, shrines, staffs, or canopies—while reciting a noble verse.
Vin_17.249: The inspection and repair of bedding and seats should be carried out by those who have gone out on these two days [of the fortnight].
Vin_17.250: One should perform the watering, sweeping, and the application of soft cow dung upon the dwelling site. Vin_17.251: One should shake out soiled bedding and seats.
Vin_17.252: If one runs excessively;
Vin_17.253: [If there is] an upward emission, it is a *saṃsṛṣṭi*;
Vin_17.254: And from that, there is the formal designation (*prajñapana*).
Vin_17.255: One should not shake out [the robe] upon a support that is dusty.
Vin_17.256: The shaking out of a single garment is permitted for those who have been well-prepared [for it]. Vin_17.257: [This applies to] a coarse [garment].
Vin_17.258. Its restoration [is as follows].

Vin_17.259. If it is impossible [to repair], having torn it into strips and tied them to a staff, one should shake it out. Vin_17.260. Even if it remains unfit for use, one should smear a hollow pillar made of cow-dung clay or plaster over a wall.
Vin_17.261: It is given for the sake of the increase of merit and for long-term endurance.
Vin_17.262: One should not, having prepared a bed, occupy it in a gateway chamber or in a palace.
Vin_17.263: One may do so in a palace on the eighth and fourteenth days as an antidote against the influx of evil.
Vin_17.264. One should maintain beds and stools.

Vin_17.265. For the sake of preventing the destruction of the hut, one should have a circular base made for the legs, cutting them short so that they do not reach the ground, and one should place it on a stand or enclose it with a frame.
Vin_17.266. One who is not a member of the Saṃgha shall not enjoy a bed or stool that has not been formally accepted by the Saṃgha through a written document.
Vin_17.267. Not on a *bhadra* seat or a *māyāṅga* seat. Vin_17.268. Not on a lamp-stand.
Vin_17.269. "Not one with many lacquered parts" means it refers to something else.
One should keep a square bolster and a pillow;
having doubled and doubled it four times, it becomes the serviceable [covering].
Vin_17.272. Filling it with cotton.
Vin_17.273. One should not prepare a bed without having inspected it. Vin_17.274. Nor without having established mindfulness.

Vin_17.275. One should not lie down on a couch or a bedding together with another person, nor in any other way. Vin_17.276. If it is impossible [to avoid], one who is modest should arrange [the bedding] separately; having placed a small rug, a bowl, a bag, or similar items between them, one should maintain mindfulness. Vin_17.277. There should be no accumulation of more than three [people]; even with assistance, one should not share the state of being mounted upon the same couch.

Vin_17.278: One should not sit on a long bench with two people. Vin_17.279: Nor should one sit with many people when no [other] seat is available. Vin_17.280: Nor should one sit on a seat together with those who have been separated by more than three years.
Vin_17.281. One may sit together with one's preceptor even inside a house, provided that one maintains mindfulness in the absence of a seat. Vin_17.282.
One must not sit together anywhere with a layperson or one who has not received ordination.

Vin_17.283. Nor with those who are eunuchs, hermaphrodites, matricides, and so forth; nor with heretics, those who have been overcome by heretics, those who live in communion through theft, those who are of different communion, or those who are not in communion.
Vin_17.284: One who has been granted the penalty of the *śikṣādattaka* [is not entitled to] participate in the communal requisites of the Saṃgha. Vin_17.285:
A *śikṣādattaka* shall occupy the position of the *ciliminī* (the mat used for confession); except at a formal assembly of the Saṃgha for the purpose of ordination (*upasampadā*).
Vin_17.286. There is no offense if, due to being caught in a narrow or crowded space, one uses a stool.

Vin_17.287. When moving bedding and seats, if there are two people, one may take hold of a bed or a bench, while the other takes hold of a mat or similar item. Vin_17.288. One should not drag or push what belongs to the Saṃgha; one should act in such a way that it does not become damaged.
There may arise an affliction from the dust of tree-pith;
one should not frequent the vicinity of these two types of unclean huts, nor should one discard waste in a forest. *Vinaya 17.289–290*
Vin_17.291: There shall be heating in the sun, drying, lancing, and the application of a probe through the openings.
Vin_17.292: The lancing of a *daṇḍaka*.
Vin_17.293: Making the middle portion of that which is depleted in the center into the middle.
Vin_17.294: It is appropriate that it be dyed.
Vin_17.295: If it cannot be restored, it should be used for lamps as wicks, even in the case of precious objects given by individuals.
Vin_17.296: Regarding that which is not otherwise useful, the application here is to smear the gems with mud onto walls, pillars, door-panels, and holes; this is the method of utilization.
Vin_17.297: [The procedure] for one who has taken [property] without hatred.
Vin_17.298: For that which remains, the Saṃgha, having assembled, shall act by striking the gaṇḍī.
Vin_17.299: One must not fail to restrain someone seen stealing property belonging to the Saṃgha.
Vin_17.300. They should not, out of fear, neglect property belonging to the Saṃgha.
Vin_17.301. [This applies to] a place that has not yet been reached. Vin_17.302.
It should not be used for other types of vessels.
Vin_17.303. If it is impossible to bring [the food] back to its original place, one may consume it by taking it to another location.
Vin_17.304. One must not consume in one location food or requisites obtained in another location.
Vin_17.305. They should give that to someone else.
Vin_17.306: Accepting the status of a slave.
Vin_17.307: When the giver does not proceed [to give].
Vin_17.308: The use of grass or wood belonging to the Saṃgha, which is one's own property that is otherwise useless, by those who are blameless.
Vin_17.309: [The distribution] is according to the order of arrival for those not assigned [specific roles], and according to seniority for those who have made use of it for their livelihood.
Vin_17.310: This applies to the requesting of assistance from them.
Vin_17.311: One should not separate that which is not dissociated from this.

Vin_17.312: This is the purification of the foot by means of water; this is its cultivation. Vin_17.313: Its entry is into the hut. Vin_17.314: One should not cause someone sitting on a seat, sitting improperly, or sitting down to rise.
Vin_17.315. There is no seniority according to age in this [matter].
Vin_17.316. One should not sit with a monk who is purified from mud or meat. Vin_17.317. One should not sit upon a wooden plank.

Vin_17.318. When there is a petitioner, one who has completed his task must not keep back an increase of food. Vin_17.319. The state of having completed the task [is established] when there is dependence on an intermediate purpose for one who is free from attachment. Vin_17.320. He should make that [food] consecrated by means of a robe or a cloth-strip intended for that purpose.

Vin_17.321: When there is a genuine need and a way [to resolve it], one should not resort to the concealment of what belongs to the Saṃgha. Vin_17.322: In such a case, if there is a true purpose, separating [the object] from this [person] is indeed blameless.
Vin_17.323: The Saṃgha should maintain her seat and her son.
Vin_17.324: And having placed barber’s tools in a basket, they should be set against a wall.
Vin_17.325: The adze, together with the axe, nail-clippers, and so forth—these are the tools.
Vin_17.326: The gift of these [tools], excluding those made of clay, is for a monk who has requested them as a loan.
Vin_17.327. A nun shall not carry glassware. Vin_17.328. She may carry any oil vessel. Vin_17.329.
[This applies to vessels] from one *kaurḍava* down to half a *kaurḍava*.
Vin_17.330. And an iron pot.
Vin_17.331. A small stool for it.
Vin_17.332. If it is made of clay, it is a vessel.
Vin_17.333. One who has received the formal agreement (saṃvṛti) [should be given] a staff.
Vin_17.334. And a carrying-net (sikya) of a single color. Vin_17.335. Should they give these two?
Vin_17.336. [The rules apply] to those who are aged and to those who are ill.
Vin_17.337. For these two, the giving [of the gift] may occur with a single utterance.
Vin_17.338. There is the carrying of a staff that makes a sound for the purpose of counteracting snakes and other such creatures.

Vin_17.339. Binding with a staff, or by striking the base with a hammer. Vin_17.340. By gnawing at the edge. Vin_17.341. One may carry an umbrella, whether it be made of wood or of variegated materials.
Vin_17.342: The staff shall be the size of a cage.
Vin_17.343: One should not travel through the midst of many villages.
Vin_17.344: If it is by way of the road, one should go with [the body] leaning to the side.
Vin_17.345. One may go out for alms while it is raining from the sky.
Vin_17.346. This does not constitute an improper act.
Vin_17.347. [The same applies] for one who is concealed by a staff.
Vin_17.348: One should leave [the robes] while staying in the houses. Vin_17.349: One should take them up when departing.

Vin_17.350: One should not frequent places where there is loud noise, brothels, taverns, royal palaces, or the quarters of Caṇḍālas, nor should one remain in a place where the *kaṭhina* robe is being suspended.
Vin_17.351. One should not dwell near a privy.
Vin_17.352. One should not dwell in the forest wearing a garment that is like a jewel. Vin_17.353. One should not [use] powdered *meruka* glass for the sake of killing living beings.
Vin_17.355: Or, the distribution of *nimba*-fruit dwellings. Vin_17.356: That its interior constitutes a superior type of equipment for that purpose. Vin_17.357: Its drying is for that same purpose.
Vin_17.358. He should be skilled in the directions, paths, lunar days, days of the week, and constellations.
Vin_17.359. He should always keep fire and water at hand.
Vin_17.360. He should store roasted flour, as well as honey and ghee, according to his ability.
Vin_17.361: If it is known that the remainder is food.
Vin_17.362: A bhikṣuṇī should not dwell in the forest. Vin_17.363: The construction of a rain-retreat house [should take place] within the city.
Vin_17.364. He should not stand at her doorway. Vin_17.365. Nor at the window. Vin_17.366. Nor at a crossroads.
Vin_17.367: Not [to go] without being clothed.
Vin_17.368: In this context, the state of being "clothed" refers to the *saṃkakṣikā* (breast-covering garment).
Vin_17.369: Nor [is it proper] to expose the arm when in the presence of a layperson.
Vin_17.370. There should be a half-lotus position in place of the full lotus position.
Vin_17.371. One should provide cloth and other items at the door of the urinal to prevent small creatures from entering.
Vin_17.372. There shall be no obstruction to the entry of nuns into the monastery.
The monks should act [as follows]. (Vin 17.374) By means of not conversing with them, and by suspending their instruction, the *poṣadha*, and the *pravāraṇā*, they should subdue them.
(Vin 17.375) Without having been granted permission, she must not enter a monk’s dwelling.
Vin_17.376: Permission is granted for a space between two true seats.
Vin_17.377: In the case of a question, there is no fault in [the monk] being defeated.
Vin_17.378: The arrangement of needles, small jars, wheels, boards, and keys for the purpose of binding within the monastery.
Vin_17.379. After the night has passed, the overseer of the monastery must inspect the dwelling.
Vin_17.380. In times of danger, he must remain awake as a watchman.
Vin_17.381. When that duty is finished, he must avoid both sleep and meditative absorption.
Vin_17.382. Regarding the completion of the arrangements here, the senior monk of the community (saṃghasthavira) shall question the steward (upadhivārika).
Vin_17.383. In the event of a theft from the monastery, if it has not been secured, the responsibility shall be assigned to the steward by those who are associated [with the matter].
Vin_17.384. In the case of a loss, [the compensation] shall consist of as many shares as there were [items lost].
Vin_17.385. One should keep a key and a bolt.
Vin_17.386. One should not depart from a door without having secured it with locks for as long as one intends to remain away.
Vin_17.387. If one enters an empty dwelling, one should perform such acts as sprinkling water [on the floor].
Vin_17.388. One should restore a disordered vessel if it can be made fit by wiping it clean. Vin_17.389.
If it is a barber’s tool, one should have it made green.
Vin_17.390. If householders should come there, one should speak with them on matters of Dharma and other such topics.
One who is capable of the Dharma should perform [the planting]. (Vin 17.391) One must not plant trees that are unsuitable. (Vin 17.392) Having planted them, one must not fail to protect them.

Vin_17.393: [The offense is incurred] by the venerable one for that tree. Vin_17.394: [It applies] to another [tree] until it bears fruit. Vin_17.395: In the case of a long duration, it is five years.
Vin_17.396. In this case, ownership belongs to the monk who has been appointed. Vin_17.397. Washing of the hands. Vin_17.398. [Washing] of the feet. [64a1]
The discarding of the tooth-stick;
the washing of the bowl and bathing—these constitute maintenance.
The construction of an inner chamber for the purpose of warding off the cold.
Vin_17.401. There should be an opening for the windows to allow for ventilation.
Vin_17.402. A covering should be provided.
Vin_17.403. If it is during the summer, it may be removed for the sake of that purpose; even in the rainy season, it may be removed until its own moisture has dried.
Vin_17.404: And they shall provide water for the drainage.
Vin_17.405: They shall not neglect their fundamental livelihood.
Vin_17.406: Having divided the maintenance work according to the two divisions of the rainy season.
In some places there was the chewing of tooth-sticks, in some the cleansing of the mouth, and in others the washing of the feet; thus, it was not due to such proliferation [of activities].
There was an assignment of duties for the monks for the protection of flowers and fruits;
for others, it was according to the time of the meal and the distance traveled.
Vin_17.410: Having eaten first, they should depart.
Vin_17.411: Even if they proceed separately, the reciter should show compassion toward those who perform more extensive services if he is unable [to do so himself].
Vin_17.412: He should show compassion by taking up that discipline (*vinaya*) through the granting of its exposition, recitation, questioning, and instruction.
The nuns should write down a letter. And they are unable to remember or retain the Vinaya.
Vin_17.415: It is not to be written down.
Vin_17.416: In the same way, here [is] the Prātimokṣa. Vin_17.417: That which is connected with it.
And [the case] of Paiṅgaliga.
(Vin_17,2,26) Making a sign regarding requisites.
Vin_17.419: Making a sign is not an offense.

Vin_17.420. The recording of the name on the bedding and seating belonging to the Saṃgha. Vin_17.421. [The formula is: "This is a gift of religious merit; this belongs to the monastery named so-and-so. Vin_17.422. And [the same applies] to robes.
And in other such cases as well:
(Vin_17,2,27) there is no imposition of the Buddha’s word upon Vedic meter.

(Vin_17.424) One should not recite or memorize the Buddha’s word by imposing it upon Vedic meter, a specific word, or a metrical sequence, even if one is capable of instructing others through external treatises that take those as their ultimate authority.
Without relinquishing his application to the word of the Buddha,
the third part of the day is designated as that time;
and so too for the night.
Vin_17.427: One should learn mantras that are beneficial. Vin_17.428: One should employ them.
Vin_17.429: Not those that are harmful.
(Vin_17,2,28) Prostration to those who have broken the Three Jewels. Vin_17.430: Among these, there is the mention of prostration as a place for the Three Jewels.
Vin_17.431: One should not prostrate to another deity.
Vin_17.432: One should not pay homage [to it]. Vin_17.433: One should not treat it with disrespect.

Vin_17.434: Standing face-to-face, one should address this verse of the Ṛṣis by reciting it; having attained the [proper] approach, one should favor [the recipient] with the sound of snapping the fingers.

One should not practice a craft. One may, however, learn one or cause another to learn it, provided that one has discarded the tools thereof: the sheath for weapons, the needle-case, and the *melaṇḍuka*.
Vin_17.438. One who is skilled in medicine should attend to a non-Buddhist ascetic with the intention of merit, without receiving any remuneration.
Vin_17.439. Having granted him solitude, one should not go elsewhere.
Vin_17.440. One may go to another monastery under such circumstances, provided there is an affliction, by making an excuse.
One may perform the duties of a barber for a fellow practitioner of the holy life who possesses similar physical characteristics, provided it is in a secluded place.
One may also repair a broken part of a bedstead,
and tie together garland strings for the sake of ornaments.
Vin_17.444: And [the rule concerning] writing refers to a painting that is not a representation of a sentient being, but serves as an object of worship for jewels.
Vin_17.445: Its reality consists in the lines representing those objects.
Vin_17.446: It concerns performing the worship of the body of a deceased fellow-practitioner of the holy life.
Vin_17.447. One may burn it, provided it does not contain living creatures or wounds.
Vin_17.448. Certainty [of its being empty] is reached through inspection.
Vin_17.449. Or one may bury it or submerge it in a river.
Vin_17.450. It is improper to place [the body] in the middle of a forest fire.
Vin_17.451. One should lie down on one’s right side with the head toward the north.
Vin_17.452. One should place the pillow upon the head.
Vin_17.453: Covering [the body] with grass or leaves.
Vin_17.454: Performing the instruction on the reward for hearing the Dharma.
Vin_17.455: Bathing with one's clothes on by those who have been touched [by an impure person].
Vin_17.456: Washing of the hands and feet by others.
Vin_17.457: Entering after having paid homage to the caitya.
Vin_17.458: There are two types [of conduct] regarding a stūpa.
Vin_17.459: It is characterized by being accompanied [by defilements] and by acting as a pillar [of support].
Vin_17.460: Arhatship is the excellence of those who have gone forth.
Vin_17.461: [It is the excellence] of all aspects for the Buddhas.
Vin_17.462: The base-platform, the four tiers, the pillar-base, the dome, the pinnacle, the thirteen parasols, and the rain-drip ledge—these are the constant forms.
Vin_17.463: For Pratyekabuddhas, there is no rain-drip ledge.
Vin_17.464: With parasols equal in number to the measure of his fruits, plus one for him, [and] for his disciples;
Vin_17.465: if there was a turning away from the side of the Tathāgata, then the making [of the image] should be in that direction where he stood when giving them that retinue.

Vin_17.466: Not in another [place], nor according to seniority. Vin_17.467: For a shaven-headed person, there is a separate distribution of vessels. Vin_17.468: This must be done outside of the monastery grounds.
Vin_17.469: One is worthy of an *ārṣa* stūpa for an Arhat.
Vin_17.470: [The property] dedicated to the stūpa of a disciple belongs to his fellow practitioners (*sabrahmacārin*).
Vin_17.471: It is lawful to construct a stūpa for the Buddha made of iron.
Vin_17.472: [The prohibition against making] stūpas for hair and nails made of gold, silver, lapis lazuli, or crystal.
Vin_17.473: The construction of a surrounding enclosure for these [stūpas] is permitted here.
Vin_17.474: The account beginning with his residence in the Tuṣita heaven and ending with his parinirvāṇa is called "The Narrative" (Vṛtta).
Vin_17.475: The giving of lime.
Vin_17.476: Whitewashing.
Vin_17.477: The acceptance of lamps.
Vin_17.478. Encircling with a railing. Vin_17.479. Erecting an archway. Vin_17.480. Hoisting banners.
Vin_17.481. This [staff] is of four kinds. Vin_17.482. Namely, the lion-bannered, the crocodile-bannered, the nāga-king-bannered, and the bull-bannered. Vin_17.483.
It may also be used in a dense forest.

Vin_17.484: The erection of an archway (toraṇa). Vin_17.485: The construction of a railing (cairaka) and its surrounding enclosure by means of a balustrade (vedikā). Vin_17.486: The coating of the pillars with red ochre (gerika).
Vin_17.487: Painting a wall with lacquer, offering perfumed consecrations, and [the offering of] oil, aloe-wood, sandalwood, and saffron sprinklings; Vin_17.488: [these are permitted]. Vin_17.489:
Planting thorns or providing ivory pegs for the purpose of hanging meat is not allowed.
Vin_17.490: Not [on] those that are broken.

Vin_17.491: No placing of lamps on top; climbing up for the purpose of honoring householders is prohibited, but in the absence [of others], novices may do so after washing their feet with scented water.
Vin_17.492: If not, then having rubbed [the body] with perfumes and wrapped it in a cloth, one should do so while keeping in mind the perception of the Teacher and reflecting upon his purpose.
The monks should treat them in exactly the same way.
For that purpose, there is the fastening with a rope and the offering of a necklace made of jewels.
Vin_17.495: Covering with a lattice-work interior to prevent [the wind] from blowing away.
Vin_17.496: Opening the doors so that there is no darkness within.
Vin_17.497: Making images of the Buddha.
Vin_17.498: There shall be no performance of the *mahā* for this [person].
Vin_17.499: And there shall be no [performance of the *mahā*] for the festivals of birth, matted hair, the top-knot, enlightenment, and the [Great] Departure.
Vin_17.500: And there shall be no making of this [announcement] upon entering a city.
Vin_17.501. In this case, it is permissible for a monk to transport that [load]. Vin_17.502. His entitlement among the novices is the granting of an entourage by the five groups. Vin_17.503.
There is the acceptance of the increase of the venerable one.
Vin_17.504: With musical instruments being played, accompanied by great and blameless honor, one should exclaim: "Play, play! O man, perform the worship of the Teacher! Vin_17.505:

There should be a proclamation in the streets, alleys, and crossroads that tomorrow or the day after tomorrow there will be the Buddha’s entry, as he proceeds with his arm raised, mounted upon the neck of an elephant, surrounded by umbrellas, banners, and flags, and with the written invitation displayed.
Vin_17.506. It is lawful to construct an image of a Bodhisattva.
Vin_17.507. Its surroundings should consist of banners, it should be encircled by a railing, and there should be iron pillars.
